"""Cap-led sector downshock overshoot with terminal absorption confirmation.

Mechanism: an abnormal-volume selloff that rejects its intrabar low is a stronger
rebound candidate when the name has already fallen more than a cap-weighted,
leave-one-out negative sector impulse.  This identifies an absorbed idiosyncratic
overshoot during common-shock propagation rather than an unfinished sector relay.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _terminal_absorption(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal abnormal-volume downside rejection score."""
    clean_ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.50, 0.50)
    clean_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    ret_scale = clean_ret.abs().rolling(window, min_periods=20).median()
    vol_scale = clean_volume.rolling(window, min_periods=20).median()
    downside = (-clean_ret).clip(lower=0.0).div(ret_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    volume_ratio = clean_volume.div(vol_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

    bar_range = (high - low).where((high - low) > 0.0)
    close_location = (close - low).div(bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    rejection = ((close_location - 0.50) / 0.50).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    score = downside.clip(0.0, 6.0) * np.log1p(volume_ratio.clip(0.0, 12.0))
    valid = ret_scale.notna() & vol_scale.notna() & bar_range.notna()
    return (score * rejection).where(valid)


def _loo_sector_state(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal leave-one-out sector impulse and cap-concentration diagnostics."""
    raw_ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    caps = market_cap.ffill().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    valid = raw_ret.notna() & caps.gt(0.0)
    weights = caps.where(valid, 0.0)

    market_den = weights.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    market_ret = raw_ret.where(valid).mul(weights).sum(axis=1).div(market_den)
    excess = raw_ret.sub(market_ret, axis=0)

    loo = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    cap = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    equal = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    labels = sector.iloc[0].reindex(close.columns) if len(sector.index) else pd.Series(index=close.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        columns = list(labels.index[labels.eq(label)])
        if not columns:
            continue

        sector_weights = weights.loc[:, columns]
        sector_excess = excess.loc[:, columns].where(valid.loc[:, columns])
        weighted_excess = sector_excess.mul(sector_weights)

        total_weight = sector_weights.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        total_weighted = weighted_excess.sum(axis=1)
        cap_daily = total_weighted.div(total_weight)

        equal_count = valid.loc[:, columns].sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        equal_daily = sector_excess.sum(axis=1).div(equal_count)

        other_weight = sector_weights.rsub(total_weight, axis=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        other_weighted = weighted_excess.rsub(total_weighted, axis=0)
        loo_daily = other_weighted.div(other_weight)

        loo.loc[:, columns] = loo_daily.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
        cap_roll = cap_daily.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
        equal_roll = equal_daily.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
        cap.loc[:, columns] = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(cap_roll.to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1),
            index=close.index,
            columns=columns,
        )
        equal.loc[:, columns] = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(equal_roll.to_numpy()[:, None], len(columns), axis=1),
            index=close.index,
            columns=columns,
        )

    own = excess.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    return loo, cap, equal, own


def _cash_resilience(
    cash: pd.DataFrame,
    liabilities: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Industry-relative balance-sheet buffer, with a neutral sparse-data fallback."""
    coverage = cash.where(cash > 0.0).div(liabilities.where(liabilities > 0.0))
    coverage = np.log1p(coverage.clip(0.0, 20.0))
    return rank(indneutralize(rank(coverage), industry)).fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class CapLeaderDownshockAbsorptionCatchup(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cap_leader_downshock_absorption_catchup"
    name = "Cap-Leader Downshock Absorption Catchup"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Terminal volume-tail downside rejection, activated only for names that "
        "overshot a concentrated leave-one-out negative sector impulse."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "sector",
        "cash",
        "totalCurrentLiabilities",
        "industry",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        low = data["low"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        sector = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        cash = data["cash"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        liabilities = data["totalCurrentLiabilities"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        industry = data["industry"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        absorption = _terminal_absorption(ret, volume, high, low, close, 60)
        loo_sector, cap_sector, equal_sector, own_sector = _loo_sector_state(
            close, market_cap, sector, 3
        )

        relay_gap = loo_sector.sub(own_sector)
        sector_down = (-loo_sector).clip(lower=0.0)
        overshoot = relay_gap.clip(lower=0.0).div(
            loo_sector.abs().add(own_sector.abs()).add(1.0e-8)
        ).clip(0.0, 2.0)
        concentration = cap_sector.abs().sub(equal_sector.abs()).div(
            cap_sector.abs().add(equal_sector.abs()).add(1.0e-8)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.75)

        downshock_overshoot = overshoot.mul(1.0 + concentration).where(sector_down > 0.0)
        relay_condition = rank(downshock_overshoot)
        resilience = _cash_resilience(cash, liabilities, industry)

        signal = rank(absorption).mul(relay_condition).mul(0.5 + 0.5 * resilience)
        return rank(signal).fillna(0.5).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Cap-Leader Downshock Absorption Catchup
programs.trading_idea: A terminal high-volume downside rejection is most credible when the stock has already overshot a contemporaneous, cap-led negative sector impulse rather than merely lagging an unfinished sector repricing. Large sector constituents transmit the common shock first, while an unusually sharp decline in a smaller constituent can represent transient liquidity displacement; a close away from the low identifies that this excess sell pressure was absorbed. The interaction has edge because the sector relay state separates absorbed relative overshoots from terminal-looking selloffs that still need to converge downward with the sector.
programs.description: Ranks abnormal-volume downside bars closing well above their lows, conditioned on the stock having underperformed a leave-one-out cap-weighted negative sector impulse and softly tilted toward industry-relative cash resilience.

"""Analyst revenue-estimate revisions can incorporate diffuse consumer-demand feedback, but investors may initially treat an upgrade as equally credible across firms. An upgrade accompanied by an improving cash-conversion cycle is more likely to represent genuine demand realization rather than channel stuffing, receivables expansion, or inventory accumulation, and should continue to drift upward; the converse should underperform. The other side is attention-constrained investors and benchmarked managers reacting to the headline consensus change while underweighting slower-to-interpret balance-sheet evidence. The mechanism is falsified if cash-conversion changes do not improve the ability of fresh estimate revisions to distinguish subsequent relative returns."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _latest_fundamental_revision(
    field: pd.DataFrame, scale_by_level: bool
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Carry forward the most recent point-in-time report-update change.

    Fundamental fields are daily forward-filled quarterly step functions.  This
    identifies genuine changes in those steps rather than treating each daily
    repetition as a new observation.  All shifts are positive-lagged and hence
    causal.
    """
    current = field.astype(float)
    previous = current.shift(1)
    updated = current.notna() & previous.notna() & current.ne(previous)

    change = current - previous
    if scale_by_level:
        change = change / previous.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    event_change = change.where(updated)
    return event_change.ffill()


def _revision_credibility_weight(
    close: pd.DataFrame, revision: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Penalize revisions already substantially confirmed by the price."""
    price_return = close.astype(float).pct_change(20)
    volatility = close.astype(float).pct_change().rolling(20, min_periods=8).std()
    standardized_move = price_return / volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    aligned_move = standardized_move * np.sign(revision)
    already_priced = aligned_move.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
    return np.exp(-already_priced).fillna(1.0)


@register_factor
class ConsumerFeedbackCashConversionRevisionGap(BaseFactor):
    """Credibility-adjusted consumer-demand estimate revision signal."""

    factor_id = "consumer_feedback_cash_conversion_revision_gap"
    name = "Consumer-Feedback Revision Credibility Gap"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks revenue-consensus revisions whose direction is corroborated by "
        "a shorter cash-conversion cycle, while discounting revisions already "
        "strongly reflected in recent prices."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = ["revenueEstimate", "cashConversionCycle", "close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        cash_conversion = data["cashConversionCycle"]
        close = data["close"]

        # Latest quarterly consensus revision, normalized by the prior consensus.
        revenue_revision = _latest_fundamental_revision(
            revenue_estimate, scale_by_level=True
        )

        # A declining cash-conversion cycle is positive confirmation.  Normalize
        # by the prior cycle magnitude so the measure is comparable across firms.
        cash_cycle_change = _latest_fundamental_revision(
            cash_conversion, scale_by_level=True
        )
        cash_confirmation = (-cash_cycle_change).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)

        credibility_adjusted_revision = revenue_revision * cash_confirmation
        price_weight = _revision_credibility_weight(close, revenue_revision)
        signal = credibility_adjusted_revision * price_weight

        return rank(signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.0)

"""Leveraged downside volatility state.

Mechanism: persistent downside volatility is more likely to be a leverage-effect
or balance-sheet repricing event for firms with weak debt capacity.  Such names
can remain under deleveraging pressure after the initial loss, producing lower
near-term returns.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _neutral_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional rank with neutral treatment of unavailable quarterly data."""
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return rank(clean).fillna(0.5)


def _downside_volatility_state(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal, scale-normalized downside loss times persistent volatility state."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close.pct_change()
    log_ret = np.log(safe_close).diff()

    realized_vol = log_ret.abs().rolling(10, min_periods=7).mean()
    slow_vol = log_ret.abs().rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean()
    persistence = (realized_vol / slow_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0)

    recent_loss = -ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    standardized_loss = (recent_loss / slow_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

    return (standardized_loss * persistence).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class LeveragedDownsideVolatilityState(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "leveraged_downside_volatility_state"
    name = "Leveraged Downside Volatility State"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "High values identify fragile balance sheets experiencing a recent "
        "downside move while realized volatility remains elevated relative to "
        "its slow baseline; these states are expected to precede lower returns."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["close", "debtToAssets", "interestCoverage", "cashRatio"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        downside_state = _downside_volatility_state(data["close"])

        debt_assets = data["debtToAssets"].clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.5)
        coverage = data["interestCoverage"].clip(lower=-10.0, upper=30.0)
        cash_ratio = data["cashRatio"].clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

        fragility = (
            _neutral_rank(debt_assets)
            + _neutral_rank(-coverage)
            + _neutral_rank(-cash_ratio)
        ) / 3.0

        pressure = downside_state * fragility
        return rank(pressure).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Downside volatility clustering is more likely to represent a persistent leverage-effect repricing when a firm's balance sheet has limited debt capacity. Rather than estimating unstable short-window return-volatility correlations, the signal identifies an ongoing state in which a recent cumulative loss coincides with volatility remaining above its slower baseline, then emphasizes firms with high debt assets, weak interest coverage, and low cash buffers. These names should experience continued deleveraging pressure over the next six daily bars, so higher factor values predict lower forward returns.
programs.description: Ranks firms by a standardized recent downside move multiplied by persistent realized-volatility elevation and a cross-sectional balance-sheet fragility score. The factor is high for financially fragile firms already in a downside volatility-clustering regime.

"""Persistent range-variance expansion as a delayed risk-regime signal.

Mechanism: a robust upward break in intraday range variance identifies a
structural transition in perceived risk.  Risk estimation, hedging, and
liquidity repricing adjust with delay, so confirmed expansions can retain
short-horizon return continuation after the initial volatility transition.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _robust_range_expansion(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robust Parkinson-variance break statistic.

    The recent and baseline windows do not overlap. Rolling medians make the
    transition measure insensitive to one-day auction, stale-price, or bad-bar
    range spikes while still requiring persistence in the recent regime.
    """
    safe_high = high.where(high > 0.0)
    safe_low = low.where(low > 0.0)
    ratio = (safe_high / safe_low).where(safe_high >= safe_low)
    log_range = np.log(ratio)
    range_variance = (log_range * log_range) / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))

    recent_level = range_variance.rolling(5, min_periods=5).median()
    baseline_level = range_variance.shift(5).rolling(30, min_periods=30).median()
    expansion = np.log(recent_level / baseline_level.replace(0.0, np.nan))

    # Only an upward state transition is supported by the observed sign;
    # cap implausibly large ratios before the final cross-sectional ranking.
    return expansion.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)


@register_factor
class RobustRangeVarianceExpansionContinuation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "robust_range_variance_expansion_continuation"
    name = "Robust Range-Variance Expansion Continuation"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Ranks persistent upward Parkinson range-variance breaks, measured by "
        "a 5-bar median relative to a non-overlapping 30-bar historical median."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        score = _robust_range_expansion(data["high"], data["low"])
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        score = score.reindex(index=data["close"].index, columns=data["close"].columns)
        return rank(score.fillna(0.0))
programs.name: Robust Range-Variance Expansion Continuation
programs.trading_idea: A sustained upward break in a stock's intraday range variance identifies a structural risk-state transition before portfolio risk estimates, hedging activity, and liquidity provision have fully adjusted. The prior implementation imposed a symmetric compression-versus-expansion interpretation, but its out-of-sample sign consistently indicated that confirmed variance expansions, rather than compressions, contain the usable six-bar continuation signal. This refinement therefore measures only persistent upward range-variance breaks using robust medians relative to each name's own older volatility regime, avoiding noisy daily sector denominators and fragile staggered-subsample confirmation branches.
programs.description: Computes Parkinson range variance, compares its recent 5-bar rolling median with a non-overlapping 30-bar historical median, and cross-sectionally ranks positive log variance expansions. Large values indicate a persistent, idiosyncratically normalized volatility-regime break.

programs.code:
"""A genuine idiosyncratic variance-regime break often forces gradual position resizing by volatility-targeting funds, market makers, and risk-constrained discretionary investors rather than an immediate full repricing. The direction of the return impulse accompanying a break should therefore continue when the break is consistently detected across several offset subsamples, whereas a break detected on only one sampling grid is more likely to be bar-noise or a transient auction effect. This implements the structural-break detection and subsampling-robustness mechanism emphasized by the source paper; it is falsified if robustly detected volatility ruptures have no directional continuation after controlling for contemporaneous sector moves."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _subsampled_semivariance_rupture(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    stride: int = 3,
    recent_window: int = 8,
    history_window: int = 40,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Estimate a robust, causal variance-break confidence across offset grids.

    Each grid observes every ``stride``-th return.  At its observation times it
    compares recent upside and downside semivariance with a preceding long-run
    semivariance estimate, then forward fills that already-observed estimate
    until the grid's next observation.  Thus staggered grids are both causal
    and resistant to a single daily-bar anomaly.
    """
    downside = ret.clip(upper=0.0).pow(2)
    upside = ret.clip(lower=0.0).pow(2)
    statistics: list[pd.DataFrame] = []

    for offset in range(stride):
        for semivariance in (downside, upside):
            sampled = semivariance.iloc[offset::stride]
            recent = sampled.rolling(recent_window, min_periods=recent_window).mean()
            history = (
                sampled.shift(recent_window)
                .rolling(history_window, min_periods=history_window)
                .mean()
            )

            valid = (recent > 1.0e-12) & (history > 1.0e-12)
            statistic = np.log(recent / history).where(valid)
            statistic = statistic.clip(lower=-6.0, upper=6.0)
            statistics.append(statistic.reindex(ret.index).ffill())

    stacked = pd.concat(statistics, axis=1, keys=range(len(statistics)))
    median_statistic = (
        stacked.T.groupby(level=1, sort=False).median().T.reindex(
            index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns
        )
    )

    agreement_numerator = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    agreement_denominator = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for statistic in statistics:
        valid = statistic.notna() & median_statistic.notna()
        same_direction = (statistic * median_statistic > 0.0).where(valid, False)
        agreement_numerator = agreement_numerator + same_direction.astype(float)
        agreement_denominator = agreement_denominator + valid.astype(float)

    agreement = agreement_numerator / agreement_denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    broad_agreement = agreement >= (2.0 / 3.0)
    magnitude = np.tanh(median_statistic.abs())
    return (magnitude * agreement).where(broad_agreement, 0.0)


def _sector_demeaned_impulse(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int = 6,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return trailing stock impulse less its contemporaneous sector impulse."""
    impulse = ret.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    groups = sector.ffill().iloc[-1].fillna("__UNKNOWN_SECTOR__")
    sector_mean = impulse.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).transform("mean").T
    return impulse - sector_mean


@register_factor
class MultiphaseSubsampledVarianceRuptureDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-relative return continuation after robust subsampled variance ruptures."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _subsampled_range_expansion(
    range_var: pd.DataFrame,
    stride: int = 3,
    recent_window: int = 6,
    history_window: int = 30,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal, staggered-subsample confirmation of upward range-variance breaks."""
    statistics: list[pd.DataFrame] = []

    for offset in range(stride):
        sampled = range_var.iloc[offset::stride]
        recent = sampled.rolling(recent_window, min_periods=recent_window).mean()
        history = (
            sampled.shift(recent_window)
            .rolling(history_window, min_periods=history_window)
            .mean()
        )
        valid = (recent > 1.0e-12) & (history > 1.0e-12)
        stat = np.log(recent / history).where(valid).clip(lower=-6.0, upper=6.0)
        statistics.append(stat.reindex(range_var.index).ffill())

    stacked = pd.concat(statistics, axis=1, keys=range(len(statistics)))
    median_stat = stacked.T.groupby(level=1, sort=False).median().T
    median_stat = median_stat.reindex(index=range_var.index, columns=range_var.columns)

    valid_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=range_var.index, columns=range_var.columns)
    expanding_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=range_var.index, columns=range_var.columns)
    for stat in statistics:
        valid = stat.notna()
        valid_count = valid_count + valid.astype(float)
        expanding_count = expanding_count + ((stat > 0.35) & valid).astype(float)

    agreement = expanding_count / valid_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    confirmed = agreement >= (2.0 / 3.0)
    magnitude = np.tanh(median_stat.clip(lower=0.0) / 2.0)
    return (magnitude * agreement).where(confirmed, 0.0)


def _market_relative_impulse(ret: pd.DataFrame, window: int = 4) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing return impulse net of the contemporaneous cross-sectional market move."""
    impulse = ret.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    return impulse.sub(impulse.mean(axis=1), axis=0)


@register_factor
class LeveredRangeRuptureOvershootReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "levered_range_rupture_overshoot_reversal"
    name = "Levered Range-Rupture Reversal"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Buy financially levered names after negative market-relative impulses and "
        "short them after positive impulses when a staggered-subsample Parkinson "
        "range-variance estimator confirms a persistent upward regime break."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "debtToEquity"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        valid_range = (high > 0.0) & (low > 0.0) & (high >= low)
        log_range = np.log(high.where(valid_range) / low.where(valid_range))
        range_var = (log_range.pow(2) / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        rupture = _subsampled_range_expansion(range_var)
        impulse = _market_relative_impulse(ret)

        leverage = data["debtToEquity"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        leverage = leverage.clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)
        leverage_rank = leverage.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.0)

        raw_score = -impulse * rupture * leverage_rank
        return raw_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)

"""Daily volume provides a coarse participation-rate proxy, while the close-to-open displacement relative to intraday range provides a proxy for realized market impact. In a calm liquidity regime, unusually high participation that produces unusually efficient directional displacement is more likely informed or persistent institutional demand and should continue; in a stressed range regime, the same excess displacement is more likely liquidity-driven overshoot and should mean revert. This implements the two-regime market-impact intuition emphasized by the source paper's discussion of transaction costs and nonlinear impact, rather than treating volume or price impact as unconditional signals. The hypothesis is falsified if impact efficiency has the same forward-return sign in calm and stressed regimes, or if conditioning on participation does not improve upon raw signed return."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_impact_residual(
    signed_impact: pd.DataFrame, participation: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal daily cross-sectional OLS residual of impact on participation."""
    valid = signed_impact.notna() & participation.notna()
    x = participation.where(valid)
    y = signed_impact.where(valid)

    count = valid.sum(axis=1)
    x_mean = x.mean(axis=1)
    y_mean = y.mean(axis=1)
    x_centered = x.sub(x_mean, axis=0)
    y_centered = y.sub(y_mean, axis=0)

    denominator = x_centered.pow(2).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = x_centered.mul(y_centered).sum(axis=1).div(denominator)
    fitted_centered = x_centered.mul(beta, axis=0)
    residual = y_centered.sub(fitted_centered)

    return residual.where(valid & count.ge(4), np.nan)


def _sector_zscore(signal: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Normalize each date's signal within static sector groups."""
    labels = sector.ffill().iloc[-1].reindex(signal.columns).astype(object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "Unknown")

    transposed = signal.T
    sector_mean = transposed.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T
    sector_std = transposed.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("std").T
    normalized = signal.sub(sector_mean).div(sector_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    return normalized.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class RegimeSplitParticipationImpactEfficiency(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-normalized residual impact, signed by the idiosyncratic range regime."""

    factor_id = "regime_split_participation_impact_efficiency"
    name = "Regime-Split Participation Impact Efficiency"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional residual of close-to-open impact versus square-root "
        "relative participation, retained in calm idiosyncratic-range regimes "
        "and reversed when the stock's range is elevated, then normalized "
        "within sector."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_price = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        bar_range = high.sub(low).abs()
        safe_range = bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        signed_impact = close.sub(open_price).div(safe_range)
        signed_impact = signed_impact.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        median_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        participation = volume.div(median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        participation = participation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=25.0)
        sqrt_participation = np.sqrt(participation)

        residual = _cross_sectional_impact_residual(signed_impact, sqrt_participation)

        relative_range = bar_range.div(close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        range_baseline = relative_range.rolling(60, min_periods=30).median()
        range_ratio = relative_range.div(range_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        regime_sign = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(range_ratio.gt(1.25), -1.0, 1.0),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        ).where(range_ratio.notna())
        regime_signal = residual.mul(regime_sign)

        return _sector_zscore(regime_signal, data["sector"])

"""State-switch between latent execution continuation and depth-collapse reversal.

Persistent under-realised participation impact is followed when liquidity is
absorbing flow normally, but fresh superlinear volume-to-range events identify
a depth-failure state in which the contemporaneous displacement is faded.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_adjusted_return(close: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal daily idiosyncratic return relative to contemporaneous industry."""
    safe_close = close.astype(float).where(close.astype(float) > 0.0)
    raw_return = (safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )
    groups = industry.iloc[0].fillna("Unknown")
    industry_return = raw_return.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).transform("mean").T
    return raw_return - industry_return


def _impact_backlog(adjusted_return: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Five-bar residual of a causal, kinked signed-participation impact curve."""
    estimation_window = 60
    minimum_observations = 40

    clean_volume = volume.astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
    median_volume = clean_volume.rolling(
        estimation_window, min_periods=minimum_observations
    ).median()
    participation = (
        clean_volume / median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)
    high_cutoff = participation.rolling(
        estimation_window, min_periods=minimum_observations
    ).quantile(0.75)

    signed_participation = np.sign(adjusted_return) * participation
    high_regime = participation > high_cutoff
    valid = adjusted_return.notna() & signed_participation.notna() & high_cutoff.notna()

    low_x = signed_participation.where(valid & ~high_regime, 0.0)
    high_x = signed_participation.where(valid & high_regime, 0.0)
    y = adjusted_return.where(valid, 0.0)

    s_ll = (low_x * low_x).rolling(estimation_window, min_periods=minimum_observations).sum()
    s_hh = (high_x * high_x).rolling(estimation_window, min_periods=minimum_observations).sum()
    s_lh = (low_x * high_x).rolling(estimation_window, min_periods=minimum_observations).sum()
    s_ly = (low_x * y).rolling(estimation_window, min_periods=minimum_observations).sum()
    s_hy = (high_x * y).rolling(estimation_window, min_periods=minimum_observations).sum()

    determinant = s_ll * s_hh - s_lh * s_lh
    beta_low = (s_hh * s_ly - s_lh * s_hy) / determinant.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta_high = (s_ll * s_hy - s_lh * s_ly) / determinant.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    expected = (beta_low * low_x + beta_high * high_x).where(valid)
    shortfall = (expected - adjusted_return).rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
    scale = adjusted_return.rolling(
        estimation_window, min_periods=minimum_observations
    ).std()
    return shortfall / scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _depth_collapse_state(
    close: pd.DataFrame, high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Identify fresh superlinear range shocks and their signed fade pressure."""
    safe_close = close.astype(float).where(close.astype(float) > 0.0)
    safe_volume = volume.astype(float).where(volume.astype(float) > 0.0)
    raw_range = ((high.astype(float) - low.astype(float)) / safe_close).where(
        high.astype(float) >= low.astype(float)
    )
    raw_range = raw_range.where(raw_range > 0.0)

    log_volume = np.log(safe_volume)
    log_range = np.log(raw_range)
    volume_base = log_volume.rolling(42, min_periods=21).median()
    range_base = log_range.rolling(42, min_periods=21).median()
    volume_surprise = log_volume - volume_base
    impact_residual = (log_range - range_base) - 0.5 * volume_surprise
    impact_state = impact_residual.rolling(3, min_periods=2).mean()

    volume_threshold = volume_surprise.rolling(42, min_periods=21).quantile(0.75)
    impact_threshold = impact_state.rolling(42, min_periods=21).quantile(0.75)
    collapse = (volume_surprise > volume_threshold) & (impact_state > impact_threshold)

    simple_return = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
    return_scale = simple_return.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std()
    signed_pressure = (
        simple_return / return_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
    severity = (1.0 + impact_state.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)).where(collapse)
    return collapse, -signed_pressure * severity


@register_factor
class DepthStateSwitchedImpactBacklog(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "depth_state_switched_impact_backlog"
    name = "Depth-State Switched Impact Backlog"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Continues industry-adjusted latent participation-impact backlog in normal "
        "depth states, but fades signed pressure during fresh superlinear depth collapses."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        adjusted_return = _industry_adjusted_return(close, data["industry"])
        backlog = _impact_backlog(adjusted_return, data["volume"])
        collapse, reversal = _depth_collapse_state(
            close, data["high"], data["low"], data["volume"]
        )

        score = backlog.where(~collapse, reversal)
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return rank(score).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Depth-State Switched Impact Backlog
programs.trading_idea: Under-realised impact from persistent high-participation flow is informative when the market is absorbing orders normally: muted displacement then represents latent metaorder demand or supply that continues to be revealed. However, when the same episode coincides with a fresh superlinear volume-to-range shock, displayed and latent depth have failed abruptly, making the signed move predominantly a temporary liquidity displacement that should reverse as depth replenishes. The interaction separates slow revelation from acute depth instability, whereas Parent A treats all impact deficits as continuation and Parent B cannot distinguish transient shocks from genuinely unfinished execution.

It follows that backlog in normal depth conditions, but switches to fading normalized signed return pressure when volume and range jointly exceed their trailing nonlinear-impact thresholds.

'''Disclosure-silent characteristic residual repair.

A stock-specific move that remains after removing the return associated with a
slow-moving operating-durability characteristic is a candidate residual
mispricing.  The repair is activated only when recent filings and estimate
fields are unchanged, making an information-based explanation less likely.
'''

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _row_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    '''Cross-sectional z-score with conservative clipping.''' 
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    mean = clean.mean(axis=1)
    std = clean.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clean.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0).clip(-3.0, 3.0)


def _industry_score(values: pd.DataFrame, industries: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    '''Industry-neutral percentile characteristic score.''' 
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    score = indneutralize(rank(clean), industries)
    return score.where(clean.notna())


def _disclosure_silence(frames: list[pd.DataFrame], window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    '''True where observed accounting/estimate fields have not changed recently.

    Changes are detected only between two valid point-in-time observations;
    thus initial missing history cannot be misclassified as disclosure silence.
    '''
    index = frames[0].index
    columns = frames[0].columns
    event = pd.DataFrame(False, index=index, columns=columns)
    known = pd.DataFrame(False, index=index, columns=columns)

    for frame in frames:
        clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        prior = clean.shift(1)
        observed_pair = clean.notna() & prior.notna()
        changed = clean.ne(prior) & observed_pair
        event = event | changed
        known = known | observed_pair

    recent_events = event.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    continuous_coverage = known.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).min()
    return recent_events.eq(0.0) & continuous_coverage.eq(1.0)


@register_factor
class DisclosureSilentCharacteristicResidualRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'disclosure_silent_characteristic_residual_repair'
    name = 'Disclosure-Silent Characteristic Residual Repair'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Fades six-bar industry-relative return residuals after removing a '
        'trailing operating-durability characteristic-factor component, but '
        'only while reported fundamentals and consensus fields are silent.'
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        'close',
        'industry',
        'grossMargin',
        'roic',
        'cashConversionCycle',
        'netDebtToEbitda',
        'revenue',
        'eps',
        'epsEstimate',
        'revenueEstimate',
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        industries = data['industry'].fillna('Unknown')

        characteristics = [
            _industry_score(data['grossMargin'], industries),
            _industry_score(data['roic'], industries),
            _industry_score(-data['cashConversionCycle'], industries),
            _industry_score(-data['netDebtToEbitda'], industries),
        ]

        composite = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        available = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for score in characteristics:
            composite = composite.add(score.fillna(0.0))
            available = available.add(score.notna().astype(float))
        composite = composite.div(available.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        exposure = _row_zscore(composite.where(available >= 3))

        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        lagged_exposure = exposure.shift(1)
        valid = lagged_exposure.notna() & daily_return.notna()
        x = lagged_exposure.where(valid)
        y = daily_return.where(valid)
        beta_raw = (x * y).sum(axis=1).div(x.pow(2).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        beta_raw = beta_raw.where(valid.sum(axis=1) >= 20)

        trailing_beta = beta_raw.ewm(halflife=25, min_periods=15, adjust=False).mean().shift(1)
        predicted_return = lagged_exposure.mul(trailing_beta, axis=0)
        residual_return = daily_return.sub(predicted_return)

        residual_move = residual_return.rolling(6, min_periods=6).sum()
        residual_vol = residual_return.rolling(40, min_periods=20).std()
        standardized_error = residual_move.div(residual_vol.mul(np.sqrt(6.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        standardized_error = standardized_error.clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        relative_error = indneutralize(standardized_error, industries)

        silent = _disclosure_silence(
            [
                data['revenue'],
                data['eps'],
                data['epsEstimate'],
                data['revenueEstimate'],
            ],
            12,
        )
        repair = (-relative_error).where(silent & exposure.notna())
        return rank(repair).fillna(0.5).reindex_like(close)

programs.trading_idea: Operating durability characteristics define a slow-moving characteristic factor structure, so part of a stock's short-horizon return should be attributable to its exposure to that common fundamental component rather than to stock-specific information. A large residual move after removing the trailing characteristic-factor component is more likely temporary mispricing when the firm has had no recent reported fundamental or estimate update to explain it. The signal therefore fades industry-relative residual dislocations only during disclosure-silent periods, preserving the original fundamental-repair mechanism while making the information-state conditioning explicit.

It removes the trailing realized return associated with that exposure, volatility-normalizes the six-bar residual displacement, and fades it only when no recent fundamental or consensus update has occurred.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor

def _robust_sector_residual(
    trailing_return: pd.DataFrame,
    characteristics: list[pd.DataFrame],
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    ridge_penalty: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    index = trailing_return.index
    columns = trailing_return.columns
    y_values = trailing_return.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    sector_values = sector.reindex(index=index, columns=columns).to_numpy(dtype=object)
    x_values = np.stack(
        [item.reindex(index=index, columns=columns).to_numpy(dtype=float) for item in characteristics],
        axis=2,
    )
    output = np.full((len(index), len(columns)), np.nan, dtype=float)
    feature_count = len(characteristics)

    for t in range(len(index)):
        y_row = y_values[t]
        x_row = x_values[t]
        sector_row = sector_values[t]
        valid = np.isfinite(y_row) & ~pd.isna(sector_row)
        if int(valid.sum()) < max(30, feature_count + 10):
            continue

        positions = np.flatnonzero(valid)
        y = y_row[valid]
        x = x_row[valid].copy()
        codes, _ = pd.factorize(sector_row[valid], sort=False)
        groups = int(codes.max()) + 1
        counts = np.bincount(codes, minlength=groups).astype(float)

        y_median = np.nanmedian(y)
        y_mad = np.nanmedian(np.abs(y - y_median))
        y_scale = max(1.4826 * y_mad, 1.0e-4)
        y = np.clip(y, y_median - 3.0 * y_scale, y_median + 3.0 * y_scale)

        for j in range(feature_count):
            values = x[:, j]
            median = np.nanmedian(values)
            if not np.isfinite(median):
                median = 0.0
            values = np.where(np.isfinite(values), values, median)
            mad = np.nanmedian(np.abs(values - median))
            scale = max(1.4826 * mad, 1.0e-6)
            x[:, j] = np.clip((values - median) / scale, -3.0, 3.0)

        y_group = np.bincount(codes, weights=y, minlength=groups) / counts
        y_within = y - y_group[codes]
        x_within = np.empty_like(x)
        for j in range(feature_count):
            group_mean = np.bincount(codes, weights=x[:, j], minlength=groups) / counts
            x_within[:, j] = x[:, j] - group_mean[codes]

        gram = x_within.T @ x_within
        rhs = x_within.T @ y_within
        system = gram + ridge_penalty * np.eye(feature_count)
        try:
            beta = np.linalg.solve(system, rhs)
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            beta = np.linalg.pinv(system) @ rhs

        residual = y_within - x_within @ beta
        residual_median = np.median(residual)
        residual_mad = np.median(np.abs(residual - residual_median))
        residual_scale = max(1.4826 * residual_mad, 1.0e-6)
        output[t, positions] = -np.clip(
            (residual - residual_median) / residual_scale,
            -4.0,
            4.0,
        )

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=index, columns=columns)


@register_factor
class RobustCharacteristicResidualReversion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'robust_characteristic_residual_reversion_h6'
    name = 'Robust Characteristic Residual Reversion'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Negative robust sector-characteristic return residuals are bought and positive residuals '
        'are sold, conditional on sufficient dollar-volume capacity and low range-based impact.'
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = [
        'close',
        'high',
        'low',
        'volume',
        'sector',
        'earningsYield',
        'freeCashFlowYield',
        'roic',
        'assetGrowth',
        'debtToEquity',
        'marketCap',
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data['high'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data['low'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data['volume'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        trailing_return = close.pct_change(5, fill_method=None)
        market_cap = data['marketCap'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        log_market_cap = np.log(market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0))

        characteristics = [
            data['earningsYield'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data['freeCashFlowYield'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data['roic'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data['assetGrowth'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data['debtToEquity'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            log_market_cap.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
        ]

        residual_alpha = _robust_sector_residual(
            trailing_return,
            characteristics,
            data['sector'],
            3.0,
        )

        dollar_volume = (close.abs() * volume.abs()).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        average_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        volume_capacity = rank(np.log1p(average_dollar_volume))

        intraday_range = (high - low).abs()
        range_impact = intraday_range / dollar_volume
        average_impact = range_impact.rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean()
        impact_capacity = 1.0 - rank(average_impact)

        execution_capacity = np.sqrt(
            volume_capacity.clip(0.0, 1.0) * impact_capacity.clip(0.0, 1.0)
        )
        tradable_signal = residual_alpha * execution_capacity
        tradable_signal = tradable_signal.where(execution_capacity > 0.10)

        return rank(tradable_signal).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

"""Option dealers' vanna hedging can amplify directional moves when a stock is near the spot level at which volatility changes most strongly alter hedge deltas. Without an option chain, this factor extracts a causal realized-smile proxy from the asymmetry between recent downside and upside semivariance, conditioned on the stock being near its medium-horizon volatility-adjusted price anchor; a negative return accompanied by a sharp downside-skew widening is interpreted as persistent negative hedge pressure, with the symmetric positive case treated positively. The other side is liquidity providers and discretionary investors who fade what appears to be an ordinary range move but do not observe the aggregate dealer gamma-vanna inventory, while the effect can persist because hedges are mechanically adjusted over several sessions. The hypothesis is falsified if skew-shock direction has no incremental predictive power after controlling for return, realized volatility, volume, and sector-relative moves."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _realized_skew_innovation(
    log_return: pd.DataFrame, short_window: int, baseline_window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal downside/upside semivariance skew shock relative to its history."""
    downside_sq = log_return.clip(upper=0.0).pow(2)
    upside_sq = log_return.clip(lower=0.0).pow(2)

    downside_var = downside_sq.rolling(
        short_window, min_periods=short_window
    ).mean()
    upside_var = upside_sq.rolling(
        short_window, min_periods=short_window
    ).mean()

    # The small floor keeps one-sided quiet windows numerically well defined
    # without allowing zero realized variance to create infinite scores.
    skew = np.log(
        (downside_var.clip(lower=1.0e-12))
        / (upside_var.clip(lower=1.0e-12))
    )
    baseline = skew.rolling(
        baseline_window, min_periods=baseline_window
    ).mean()
    return skew - baseline


def _zero_vanna_anchor_gate(
    log_price: pd.DataFrame, log_return: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Smoothly weights observations close to a volatility-scaled price anchor."""
    anchor = log_price.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    horizon_volatility = (
        log_return.rolling(window, min_periods=window).std() * np.sqrt(window)
    ).clip(lower=1.0e-6)
    anchor_distance = (log_price - anchor) / horizon_volatility
    return np.exp(-0.5 * anchor_distance.clip(lower=-6.0, upper=6.0).pow(2))


@register_factor
class ZeroVannaRealizedSkewHedgePressure(BaseFactor):
    """Directional realized-smile shock near a volatility-adjusted price anchor."""

    factor_id = "zero_vanna_realized_skew_hedge_pressure"
    name = "Zero-Vanna Realized Skew Hedge Pressure"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of directional realized-semivariance skew shocks, "
        "weighted by a recent signed move and a smooth zero-vanna-style price "
        "anchor gate. Negative downside-skew shocks after declines indicate "
        "persistent negative dealer hedge pressure; upside analogues are positive."
    )
    window_length = 100
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        log_price = np.log(safe_close)
        log_return = log_price.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        skew_innovation = _realized_skew_innovation(
            log_return, short_window=10, baseline_window=60
        )

        # A short cumulative move measures the hedge-rebalancing direction in
        # volatility units, rather than allowing high-volatility names to dominate.
        recent_move = log_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        short_volatility = (
            log_return.rolling(10, min_periods=10).std() * np.sqrt(3.0)
        ).clip(lower=1.0e-6)
        standardized_move = recent_move / short_volatility

        anchor_gate = _zero_vanna_anchor_gate(log_price, log_return, window=40)

        # Orient the smile shock toward the tail associated with the move.
        # For a decline, downside-skew widening is negative pressure; for an
        # advance, upside-skew widening (a lower down/up ratio) is positive.
        directional_skew = -np.sign(standardized_move) * skew_innovation
        pressure = standardized_move * directional_skew * anchor_gate
        pressure = pressure.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        return rank(pressure).fillna(0.5)

"""Seasoned realized-skew convexity unwind.

Mechanism: a downside realized-semivariance acceleration relative to a seasoned
variance baseline approximates a variance-swap convexity shock.  When this
shock occurs near a volatility-scaled price anchor, zero-vanna-style hedge
adjustments are prone to fade rather than extend the initial selloff, creating
a short-horizon reversal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _seasoned_skew_unwind(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal fast-versus-seasoned semivariance shock near a price anchor."""
    log_price = np.log(close.where(close > 0.0))
    ret = log_price.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    down_sq = ret.clip(upper=0.0).pow(2)
    up_sq = ret.clip(lower=0.0).pow(2)

    # EWM estimates avoid a hard rolling-window boundary while retaining a
    # distinctly short shock scale and a seasoned historical variance scale.
    fast_down = down_sq.ewm(halflife=8, min_periods=10, adjust=False).mean()
    fast_up = up_sq.ewm(halflife=8, min_periods=10, adjust=False).mean()
    slow_down = down_sq.ewm(halflife=32, min_periods=40, adjust=False).mean()
    slow_up = up_sq.ewm(halflife=32, min_periods=40, adjust=False).mean()

    floor = 1.0e-10
    fast_skew = np.log((fast_down + floor) / (fast_up + floor))
    seasoned_skew = np.log((slow_down + floor) / (slow_up + floor))
    skew_acceleration = (fast_skew - seasoned_skew).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

    recent_move = ret.rolling(5, min_periods=4).sum()
    seasoned_vol = np.sqrt((slow_down + slow_up) * 5.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    downside_impulse = (-recent_move / seasoned_vol).clip(0.0, 3.0)

    anchor = log_price.ewm(halflife=20, min_periods=40, adjust=False).mean()
    anchor_scale = np.sqrt((slow_down + slow_up) * 20.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    anchor_distance = ((log_price - anchor) / anchor_scale).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
    anchor_gate = np.exp(-0.5 * anchor_distance.pow(2))

    valid = slow_down.notna() & slow_up.notna() & recent_move.notna()
    signal = (
        downside_impulse
        * skew_acceleration.clip(lower=0.0)
        * anchor_gate
    ).where(valid)
    return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class SeasonedSemivarianceVannaUnwind(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "seasoned_semivariance_vanna_unwind"
    name = "Seasoned Semivariance Vanna Unwind"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Ranks downside realized-skew accelerations against a seasoned variance "
        "baseline, concentrated near a volatility-scaled price anchor where "
        "convexity hedging pressure is expected to unwind."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        signal = _seasoned_skew_unwind(data["close"])
        return rank(signal).fillna(0.5)

Near a medium-term price anchor, zero-vanna-style hedge sensitivity is most likely to change sign or decay, so the initial selloff is more likely to be mechanically over-hedged than to continue. The prior implementation's negative realized IC supports this unwind interpretation at six days: the informative component is the convexity-correction reversal after a downside skew shock, not fragile-flow continuation.

High values indicate downside convexity shocks expected to unwind over the next six bars.

"""Investors often treat a reported gross-margin or cost-of-revenue change as a noisy, temporary input-cost fluctuation, especially for firms with historically unstable cost intensity. When the stock's recent sector-relative reaction is materially smaller than the standardized disclosed cost shock, the market has not fully incorporated the implied change in operating profitability and subsequent returns should drift in the shock direction. The trade is against investors and mandates that rationally avoid aggressively trading noisy quarterly cost data, while the mispricing persists because the distinction between transitory cost noise and persistent margin deterioration is resolved gradually; the factor-timing paper also motivates using a stable, low-turnover quarterly state rather than rapidly retiming the exposure. It would be falsified if standardized cost shocks are immediately incorporated into sector-relative prices, leaving no subsequent relation between the residual reaction gap and six-day returns."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _quarterly_cost_shock(
    cost_of_revenue: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute a causal standardized change in reported cost intensity.

    Fundamental inputs are point-in-time, forward-filled quarterly step
    functions. A nonzero cost-intensity difference identifies a fresh report
    update; the shock is standardized against the prior trailing history of
    report-level changes, rather than against repeated daily step values.
    """
    safe_revenue = revenue.where(revenue.abs() > 1.0e-12)
    intensity = (cost_of_revenue / safe_revenue).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    intensity = intensity.where(intensity.abs() <= 10.0)

    raw_change = intensity.diff()
    report_update = raw_change.abs() > 1.0e-12
    report_change = raw_change.where(report_update)

    prior_mean = report_change.rolling(504, min_periods=2).mean().shift(1)
    prior_std = report_change.rolling(504, min_periods=2).std(ddof=1).shift(1)
    standardized = (report_change - prior_mean) / prior_std.where(prior_std > 1.0e-8)

    # Sparse quarterly histories often lack enough observations for a stable
    # standard deviation. Use a bounded scale based on prior change magnitude.
    robust_scale = report_change.abs().rolling(504, min_periods=2).mean().shift(1)
    fallback = report_change / robust_scale.where(robust_scale > 1.0e-8)
    shock = standardized.where(standardized.notna(), fallback)
    shock = shock.clip(-6.0, 6.0)

    # A decline in costs/revenue is favorable, hence invert the cost shock.
    favorable_shock = -shock
    return favorable_shock, report_update


def _sector_relative_reaction(
    close: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing six-bar return less the contemporaneous sector mean return."""
    ret_6 = close.pct_change(6).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    sector_labels = sector.ffill().bfill()
    sector_mean = ret_6.T.groupby(sector_labels.iloc[-1] if len(sector_labels) else pd.Series(dtype=object)).transform("mean").T

    # Sector labels are static by contract, but calculate each date defensively
    # so panel alignment remains correct if a feed contains intermittent labels.
    sector_mean = ret_6.copy() * np.nan
    for timestamp in ret_6.index:
        labels = sector_labels.loc[timestamp]
        sector_mean.loc[timestamp] = ret_6.loc[timestamp].groupby(labels).transform("mean")
    return ret_6 - sector_mean


@register_factor
class CostVariancePriceDecouplingDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks favorable cost shocks whose sector-relative price reaction is too small."""

    factor_id = "cost_variance_price_decoupling_drift"
    name = "Cost-Uncertainty Price-Decoupling Drift"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "At each point-in-time cost report update, standardizes the change in "
        "costOfRevenue/revenue against prior report changes and subtracts the "
        "recent sector-relative price reaction. Long favorable cost shocks that "
        "received too little appreciation and short adverse shocks that received "
        "too little decline, with report-age and shock-size downweighting."
    )
    window_length = 510
    inputs = ["close", "costOfRevenue", "revenue", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        cost_of_revenue = data["costOfRevenue"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        favorable_shock, report_update = _quarterly_cost_shock(cost_of_revenue, revenue)
        relative_reaction = _sector_relative_reaction(close, sector)

        # Positive residual means the favorable profit implication exceeds the
        # already-observed sector-adjusted repricing; negative is symmetric.
        residual_gap = favorable_shock - relative_reaction
        shock_weight = favorable_shock.abs().clip(upper=3.0) / 3.0

        # Carry the report signal only briefly after disclosure; this captures
        # gradual assimilation while avoiding stale quarterly information.
        event_signal = (residual_gap * shock_weight).where(report_update)
        stable_signal = event_signal.ffill(limit=15)
        stable_signal = stable_signal.where(stable_signal.notna(), 0.0)

        return rank(stable_signal).fillna(0.5)
