"""Stable reciprocal peer-information diffusion response gap.

Mechanism: common information and index-flow shocks can arrive first in some
industry peers and only subsequently in follower names.  A lagged peer shock is
used only when its relation to the stock has been stable across adjacent samples
and its reverse relation corroborates a shared propagation channel rather than a
one-off correlation accident.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(frame: pd.DataFrame, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.Series:
    """Extract static metadata labels, isolating names without a label."""
    aligned = frame.reindex(columns=columns).ffill().bfill()
    fallback = pd.Series(
        [f"__unknown_{ticker}" for ticker in columns], index=columns, dtype=object
    )
    if aligned.empty:
        return fallback
    labels = aligned.iloc[0].where(aligned.iloc[0].notna(), fallback)
    return labels.astype(str)


def _group_transform(
    values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, operation: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date group transform, without any time-series mixing."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform(operation).T


def _leave_one_out_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """Available-observation leave-one-out group mean and static eligibility."""
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    valid = clean.notna().astype(float)
    group_sum = _group_transform(clean.fillna(0.0), labels, "sum")
    group_count = _group_transform(valid, labels, "sum")

    peer_sum = group_sum - clean.fillna(0.0)
    peer_count = group_count - valid
    peers = peer_sum / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    membership = pd.Series(1.0, index=values.columns).groupby(
        labels, sort=False
    ).transform("sum")
    eligible = membership >= 3.0
    return peers.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan), eligible


def _stable_peer_gap(
    stock_residual: pd.DataFrame, peer_residual: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal lag-one forecast error with persistence and reciprocity shrinkage.

    The response beta and all confidence quantities are delayed one bar before
    being applied, so the forecast available at t uses only relationships known
    by t-1.  Adjacent 30-bar correlations provide a smooth persistence measure;
    a reciprocal correlation that is grossly inconsistent with the forward one
    receives little weight.
    """
    lagged_peer = peer_residual.shift(1)
    lagged_stock = stock_residual.shift(1)

    cov = stock_residual.rolling(60, min_periods=60).cov(lagged_peer)
    peer_var = lagged_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=60).var()
    beta = (cov / peer_var.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)

    forward_recent = stock_residual.rolling(30, min_periods=30).corr(lagged_peer)
    forward_prior = forward_recent.shift(30)
    reverse_recent = peer_residual.rolling(30, min_periods=30).corr(lagged_stock)

    same_sign = (forward_recent * forward_prior > 0.0).astype(float)
    persistence = (
        np.minimum(forward_recent.abs(), forward_prior.abs())
        / np.maximum(forward_recent.abs(), forward_prior.abs()).add(0.03)
    )
    reciprocity = 1.0 - (
        (forward_recent - reverse_recent).abs()
        / (forward_recent.abs() + reverse_recent.abs() + 0.08)
    )
    confidence = (
        forward_recent.abs() * persistence * reciprocity.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        * same_sign
    ).shift(1)

    implied = beta.shift(1) * lagged_peer
    paid_response = stock_residual
    own_vol = stock_residual.rolling(30, min_periods=30).std()
    gap = (implied - paid_response) / own_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (gap * confidence).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class ReciprocityValidatedPeerResponseGap(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks the unpaid response to a stable lagged industry-peer innovation."""

    factor_id = "reciprocity_validated_peer_response_gap"
    name = "Reciprocity-Validated Peer Response Gap"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral leave-one-out industry peer shocks forecast a stock's "
        "residual return only when lagged dependence is persistent and "
        "reciprocally corroborated; the factor ranks the unpaid response gap."
    )
    window_length = 100
    inputs = ["close", "sector", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        raw_return = (close / prior_close - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        lower = raw_return.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
        upper = raw_return.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
        clipped_return = raw_return.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)

        sector_labels = _static_labels(data["sector"], close.columns)
        industry_labels = _static_labels(data["industry"], close.columns)
        sector_component = _group_transform(clipped_return, sector_labels, "median")
        residual = (clipped_return - sector_component).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        peer_residual, eligible = _leave_one_out_mean(residual, industry_labels)
        signal = _stable_peer_gap(residual, peer_residual).where(eligible, np.nan)
        return rank(signal).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Reciprocity-Validated Peer Response Gap
programs.trading_idea: Economically related stocks can incorporate common information at different speeds after sector-wide moves have been removed. A lagged industry-peer shock is most informative when its lead-lag relation has persisted across adjacent trailing samples and is corroborated by a non-contradictory reverse relationship, rather than arising from a single accidental correlation episode. Names whose current idiosyncratic return remains below their stable peer-implied response should subsequently catch up, while already-overresponding names should lag.
programs.description: The signal removes robust same-day sector returns, forms leave-one-out industry residual baskets, estimates a lag-one peer-response beta, and ranks the volatility-scaled unpaid response gap. The beta is used with a one-bar delay and is shrunk by rolling stability and reciprocity confirmation.

"""Confirmed earnings surprises following aligned anticipatory trading.

Mechanism: coherent directional trading before an earnings release can proxy for
anticipatory or informed positioning.  When the fresh disclosed EPS surprise
confirms that direction, public-information assimilation is incomplete and the
confirmed direction should continue over the next several daily bars.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_confirmed_report(
    surprise: pd.DataFrame, actual: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag a newly available EPS surprise jointly confirmed by reported EPS."""
    surprise_changed = surprise.notna() & (
        surprise.ne(surprise.shift(1)) | surprise.shift(1).isna()
    )
    actual_changed = actual.notna() & (
        actual.ne(actual.shift(1)) | actual.shift(1).isna()
    )
    return (surprise_changed & actual_changed).astype(float)


def _pre_event_flow_balance(
    close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal signed participation balance over the ten bars before today.

    Each prior return contributes only its sign, weighted by relative traded
    volume.  The ratio is near +/-1 when participation was persistently one
    sided and near zero when trading was directionally mixed.  Both price and
    volume channels are shifted first, excluding report-day activity.
    """
    prior_return = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).shift(1)
    prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
    volume_baseline = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).median().shift(1)
    relative_volume = prior_volume / volume_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    participation = relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

    signed_flow = np.sign(prior_return) * participation
    numerator = signed_flow.rolling(10, min_periods=7).sum()
    denominator = signed_flow.abs().rolling(10, min_periods=7).sum()
    return numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class ReportAlignedAnticipatoryFlowDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "report_aligned_anticipatory_flow_drift"
    name = "Report-Aligned Anticipatory Flow Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Trades fresh EPS surprises only when the surprise direction confirms "
        "a coherent ten-bar, pre-event volume-weighted directional-flow balance."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "epsSurprise", "epsActual"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        surprise = data["epsSurprise"].astype(float)
        actual = data["epsActual"].astype(float)

        fresh = _fresh_confirmed_report(surprise, actual)

        # Require a minimally broad same-day event cohort so cross-sectional
        # surprise ranks are not determined by a handful of observations.
        cohort_ok = (fresh.sum(axis=1) >= 5).astype(float)
        active = fresh.mul(cohort_ok, axis=0)

        # Price scaling makes EPS surprises comparable across different share
        # price and EPS scales while retaining the economically relevant sign.
        scaled_surprise = surprise / close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        surprise_rank = rank(scaled_surprise.where(active > 0.0))
        surprise_direction = 2.0 * surprise_rank - 1.0

        pre_flow = _pre_event_flow_balance(close, volume)
        alignment = (surprise_direction * pre_flow).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        raw = surprise_direction * alignment

        # Preserve surprise direction while ranking only the strength of
        # confirmed alignment.  Non-events and unconfirmed flow remain neutral.
        eligible = (active > 0.0) & (alignment > 0.0)
        strength = rank(raw.abs().where(eligible))
        signal = np.sign(raw) * strength
        return signal.fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Report-Aligned Anticipatory Flow Drift
programs.trading_idea: Pre-report trading is most informative when its direction, rather than merely its concentration, agrees with the subsequently disclosed earnings surprise. Persistent volume-weighted directional pressure before a report can reflect information leakage or anticipatory positioning; a fresh public surprise confirming that direction validates the latent signal and leaves slower investors to complete their repricing over the following week. The factor therefore trades only confirmed surprise events and gives greater weight to disclosures aligned with coherent pre-event flow.
programs.description: On fresh EPS report updates, the factor ranks price-scaled surprise direction and weights it by the positive alignment between the surprise and a trailing, pre-event volume-weighted directional-flow balance. Current-day price and volume are excluded from the flow estimate.

"""Fundamental-surprise drift conditional on accepted, structured market impact."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _transition_entropy(states: pd.DataFrame, window: int, n_states: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal normalized conditional entropy of discrete trailing transitions."""
    previous = states.shift(1)
    valid = states.notna() & previous.notna()
    valid_count = valid.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()

    total = valid.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    safe_total = total.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)

    for source in range(n_states):
        source_count = (
            (previous.eq(source) & valid)
            .astype(float)
            .rolling(window, min_periods=1)
            .sum()
        )
        safe_source = source_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        for destination in range(n_states):
            count = (
                (previous.eq(source) & states.eq(destination) & valid)
                .astype(float)
                .rolling(window, min_periods=1)
                .sum()
            )
            joint_probability = count / safe_total
            conditional_probability = count / safe_source
            term = joint_probability * np.log(
                conditional_probability.where(count > 0.0)
            )
            entropy = entropy - term.fillna(0.0)

    entropy = entropy / np.log(float(n_states))
    return entropy.where(valid_count >= 40.0)


def _return_volume_states(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Six causal states combining return sign and relative-volume regime."""
    ret = close.replace(0.0, np.nan).pct_change(fill_method=None)
    normal_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
    relative_volume = volume / normal_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    direction = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(ret > 0.0, 2.0, np.where(ret < 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)),
        index=close.index,
        columns=close.columns,
    )
    activity = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(relative_volume > 1.0, 1.0, 0.0),
        index=close.index,
        columns=close.columns,
    )
    states = direction * 2.0 + activity
    return states.where(ret.notna() & relative_volume.notna())


def _fresh_standardized_surprise(surprise: pd.DataFrame, lookback: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time report update standardized only by prior available history."""
    prior = surprise.shift(1)
    updated = surprise.notna() & (prior.isna() | surprise.ne(prior))
    historical_scale = surprise.abs().rolling(lookback, min_periods=20).median().shift(1)
    fallback = surprise.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    scale = historical_scale.where(historical_scale > 0.0, fallback)
    standardized = surprise / scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return standardized.where(updated, 0.0).fillna(0.0)


def _matured_reversal(
    residual: pd.DataFrame,
    excess: pd.DataFrame,
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    maturity: int,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal weighted reversal fraction for fully matured prior impact shocks."""
    old_residual = residual.shift(maturity)
    old_excess = excess.shift(maturity)
    realized_path = ret.rolling(maturity, min_periods=maturity).sum()

    weights = old_excess.abs().clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
    payoff = (
        -np.sign(old_residual) * realized_path
        / old_residual.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0)
    valid = weights.notna() & payoff.notna() & weights.gt(0.0)

    numerator = (weights * payoff).where(valid, 0.0).rolling(window, min_periods=60).sum()
    denominator = weights.where(valid, 0.0).rolling(window, min_periods=60).sum()
    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(denominator >= 4.0)


def _sector_rank(signal: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank within each static sector."""
    labels = sector.iloc[0].astype(object).where(sector.iloc[0].notna(), "Unknown")
    return signal.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True).T


@register_factor
class SurpriseFlowImpactAcceptanceDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Trade report-surprise drift only when the price impact is accepted."""

    factor_id = "surprise_flow_impact_acceptance_drift"
    name = "Surprise Flow Impact Acceptance"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Within-sector report-surprise drift conditioned on predictable high-participation "
        "flow and accepted rather than transient square-root market impact."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)

        states = _return_volume_states(close, volume)
        entropy = _transition_entropy(states, 60, 6)
        predictability = (1.0 - entropy).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        eps_event = _fresh_standardized_surprise(data["epsSurprise"], 126)
        revenue_event = _fresh_standardized_surprise(data["revenueSurprise"], 126)
        event_count = eps_event.ne(0.0).astype(float) + revenue_event.ne(0.0).astype(float)
        fresh_surprise = ((eps_event + revenue_event) / event_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)
        decayed_surprise = (
            fresh_surprise
            + 0.60 * fresh_surprise.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
            + 0.30 * fresh_surprise.shift(2).fillna(0.0)
        )
        event_active = decayed_surprise.ne(0.0)

        normal_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().shift(1)
        relative_volume = volume / normal_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        participation = (
            relative_volume.rolling(3, min_periods=1).max() - 1.0
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        root_participation = np.sqrt(relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=25.0))

        impact_per_root = ret.abs() / root_participation.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impact_coefficient = impact_per_root.rolling(126, min_periods=50).median().shift(1)
        expected_impact = impact_coefficient * root_participation
        residual = np.sign(ret) * (ret.abs() - expected_impact)
        residual_scale = residual.abs().rolling(126, min_periods=50).median().shift(1)
        standardized_residual = residual / residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        excess = np.sign(residual) * (standardized_residual.abs() - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        up_rejection = ((high - close).clip(lower=0.0) / bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        down_rejection = ((close - low).clip(lower=0.0) / bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        directional_rejection = up_rejection.where(residual >= 0.0, down_rejection).fillna(0.0)

        reversal = _matured_reversal(
            residual, excess, ret, self.prediction_horizon, 180
        ).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.5)
        transient_risk = (
            excess.abs().clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0) / 3.0
        ) * directional_rejection * (0.4 + 0.4 * reversal)
        acceptance = (1.0 - transient_risk).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        surprise_alignment = np.sign(decayed_surprise) * np.sign(ret)
        alignment_gate = (0.5 + 0.5 * surprise_alignment).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.5)
        raw_signal = (
            decayed_surprise
            * predictability.fillna(0.0)
            * participation.fillna(0.0)
            * acceptance.fillna(0.0)
            * alignment_gate
        )

        ranked = _sector_rank(raw_signal.fillna(0.0), data["sector"]) - 0.5
        active = event_active & predictability.notna() & participation.gt(0.0) & acceptance.gt(0.0)
        return ranked.where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Surprise Flow Impact Acceptance
programs.trading_idea: Fresh earnings or revenue surprises should drift only when the associated trading flow is structured and the price move is accepted by available liquidity rather than rejected as a temporary traversal of shallow depth. The child goes long positive surprises and short negative surprises when return-volume transitions are predictable, participation is elevated, and the current move lies near its normal square-root impact curve with little directional wick rejection or historically observed shock reversal. Parent A identifies informed directional flow but can mistake thin-book overreaction for information, while Parent B identifies transient impact but has no fundamental direction; their interaction isolates fundamental information whose market-impact footprint appears permanent.
programs.description: The signal ranks fresh standardized report surprises after conditioning them on low Markov transition entropy, elevated relative-volume participation, and an impact-acceptance gate based on square-root impact residuals, wick rejection, and matured reversal behavior. Transient excess-impact report reactions are suppressed rather than faded independently of the surprise.

"""Cash-resilient firms can rebound rapidly after acute relative selloffs.

Mechanism: industry-relative price pressure from de-risking or benchmark flow is
more likely temporary when the latest public accounts still show cash
realization, liquidity, low leverage, and profitable operations.  Concentrating
on recent, sign-consistent displacement targets the short repair interval rather
than the slower valuation convergence of a long-horizon drawdown."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _resilience_score(
    income_quality: pd.DataFrame,
    operating_cash_flow_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    current_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_equity: pd.DataFrame,
    operating_margin: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Sparse-field robust cross-sectional accounting resilience composite."""
    components = [
        rank(income_quality.clip(-3.0, 3.0)),
        rank(operating_cash_flow_growth.clip(-2.0, 2.0)),
        rank(current_ratio.clip(0.0, 10.0)),
        rank((-debt_to_equity).clip(-10.0, 10.0)),
        rank(operating_margin.clip(-1.0, 1.0)),
    ]

    total = components[0].fillna(0.0)
    count = components[0].notna().astype(float)
    for component in components[1:]:
        total = total + component.fillna(0.0)
        count = count + component.notna().astype(float)

    score = total / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return score.where(count >= 3.0)


@register_factor
class CashResilienceAcuteRelativeSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Fades acute industry-relative extremes conditional on cash resilience."""

    factor_id = "cash_resilience_acute_relative_snapback"
    name = "Cash-Resilient Acute Relative Snapback"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Long cash-resilient firms with an acute, continuing industry-relative "
        "selloff and short financially fragile firms with a corresponding runup."
    )
    window_length = 42
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "incomeQuality",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
        "operatingMargin",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        medium_return = close / close.shift(21).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        recent_return = close / close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0

        medium_relative = indneutralize(medium_return, industry)
        recent_relative = indneutralize(recent_return, industry)

        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        volatility = daily_return.rolling(21, min_periods=15).std()
        medium_scaled = medium_relative / (volatility * np.sqrt(21.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        recent_scaled = recent_relative / (volatility * np.sqrt(5.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        displacement = 2.0 * rank(medium_scaled.clip(-5.0, 5.0)) - 1.0
        resilience = 2.0 * rank(
            _resilience_score(
                data["incomeQuality"],
                data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"],
                data["currentRatio"],
                data["debtToEquity"],
                data["operatingMargin"],
            )
        ) - 1.0

        # A sign-consistent recent move identifies an unresolved acute shock.
        # Its bounded magnitude prevents an isolated last-bar move from
        # dominating the medium displacement measurement.
        continuation = (recent_scaled.abs() / 1.5).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        same_direction = (medium_scaled * recent_scaled > 0.0).astype(float)
        acute_gate = continuation * same_direction

        long_leg = resilience.clip(lower=0.0) * (-displacement).clip(lower=0.0)
        short_leg = (-resilience).clip(lower=0.0) * displacement.clip(lower=0.0)
        signal = (long_leg - short_leg) * acute_gate

        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        ).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Cash-Resilient Acute Relative Snapback
programs.trading_idea: Temporary industry-relative selloffs should reverse more quickly over a six-day horizon when the firm has recently disclosed durable cash realization, balance-sheet liquidity, low leverage, and operating profitability. The original long-horizon displacement likely captured a slower valuation repair, so this refinement isolates an acute, still-continuing relative price shock while retaining the same fundamental-resilience confirmation. It shorts the mirror image: financially fragile firms experiencing an acute industry-relative runup.
programs.description: The signal combines a sparse-field-robust cash-resilience composite with standardized 21-day industry-relative displacement, gated by a sign-consistent five-day relative move. It is long resilient acute relative losers and short fragile acute relative winners.

"""Peer compensator conditioned on locally absorbed counterflow.

Mechanism: lagged peer order-flow pressure can transmit across economically
related names, but its delayed target response is especially reliable when the
target's own coherent flow was absorbed with little displacement.  Such local
impact deficits proxy dealer inventory transfer; the parent evidence indicates
that their subsequent price effect is opposite the original local flow.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _loo_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-one-out static-industry mean, computed independently each date."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    aligned = labels.reindex(values.columns).fillna("Unknown")
    for group in pd.unique(aligned):
        members = aligned.index[aligned == group]
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        block = values.loc[:, members]
        out.loc[:, members] = (
            block.sum(axis=1).to_numpy()[:, None] - block.to_numpy()
        ) / float(len(members) - 1)
    return out


def _partial_peer_beta(
    response: pd.DataFrame,
    peer_state: pd.DataFrame,
    own_flow: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal ridge partial beta of response on peer state controlling own flow."""
    minimum = window // 2
    mx = peer_state.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()
    mz = own_flow.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()
    my = response.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()
    vx = (peer_state * peer_state).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean() - mx * mx
    vz = (own_flow * own_flow).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean() - mz * mz
    cxy = (peer_state * response).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean() - mx * my
    czy = (own_flow * response).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean() - mz * my
    cxz = (peer_state * own_flow).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean() - mx * mz
    ridge = 0.05
    avx = vx.clip(lower=0.0) + ridge
    avz = vz.clip(lower=0.0) + ridge
    det = (avx * avz - cxz * cxz).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = (cxy * avz - czy * cxz) / det
    return beta.shift(1).clip(-2.0, 2.0)


@register_factor
class AbsorbedCounterflowPeerCompensatorH6(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "absorbed_counterflow_peer_compensator_h6"
    name = "Absorbed Counterflow Peer Compensator"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Industry peer-flow unpaid-response gap, activated only when a target's "
        "coherent low-impact local flow implies a reversal in the same direction."
    )
    window_length = 100
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        labels = data["industry"].ffill().iloc[-1].reindex(close.columns).fillna("Unknown")

        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        peer_ret = _loo_mean(ret, labels)
        idio_ret = ret - peer_ret
        idio_vol = idio_ret.rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        response = (idio_ret / idio_vol).clip(-5.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        clv = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=25).median()
        abnormal = (volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(0.0, 6.0)
        signed_flow = (clv * abnormal).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        flow_mean = signed_flow.rolling(60, min_periods=30).mean()
        flow_std = signed_flow.rolling(60, min_periods=30).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        own_flow = ((signed_flow - flow_mean) / flow_std).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)
        peer_state = _loo_mean(own_flow, labels).shift(1).rolling(3, min_periods=2).mean().fillna(0.0)
        beta_peer = _partial_peer_beta(response, peer_state, own_flow, 80).fillna(0.0)
        beta_own = _partial_peer_beta(response, own_flow, peer_state, 80).fillna(0.0)
        peer_gap = beta_peer * peer_state + beta_own * own_flow - response

        cum_flow = signed_flow.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        flow_mass = signed_flow.abs().rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        coherence = (cum_flow.abs() / flow_mass.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        log_close = np.log(close)
        realized = log_close - log_close.shift(5)
        historical_impact = (
            realized.abs().shift(1)
            / cum_flow.abs().shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).rolling(60, min_periods=24).median()
        expected_impact = cum_flow.abs() * historical_impact
        along_flow = np.sign(cum_flow) * realized
        deficit = ((expected_impact - along_flow) / expected_impact.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 2.0)
        local_reversal = -np.sign(cum_flow) * coherence.fillna(0.0) * deficit.fillna(0.0)

        agreement = (np.sign(local_reversal) * np.sign(peer_gap)).clip(lower=0.0)
        local_strength = local_reversal.abs().clip(0.0, 1.0)
        activation = agreement * local_strength
        signal = peer_gap * activation
        return rank(signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Absorbed Counterflow Peer Compensator
programs.trading_idea: Peer-flow unpaid-response signals are most credible when the target is simultaneously experiencing coherent local flow that has been absorbed with unusually little price impact. Parent A's negative realized sign implies that an unpriced local flow cluster is predominantly temporary inventory transfer rather than directional information: its eventual unwind is opposite to the local flow direction. The child trades a peer-implied catch-up only when that expected direction agrees with the target's locally absorbed counterflow reversal, identifying names where industry-level information pressure and local dealer-inventory normalization reinforce each other.
programs.description: Computes an industry leave-one-out lagged peer-flow response compensator, controlling for the target's own flow, then conditions it on a coherent five-bar close-location-weighted abnormal-volume cluster with an unusually low realized impact. The local cluster enters only as an agreement gate in its empirically indicated reversal direction rather than as an unconditional directional-flow continuation signal.

programs.code:
"""Fast-horizon repair of stable same-industry relative-price spreads.

Mechanism: a peer-relative price residual is tradable over six daily bars only
when its own direct error-correction process has a short, stable half-life.
The factor buys negative residuals and sells positive residuals, but excludes
slow or structurally unstable peer relationships whose convergence occurs too
late for the forecast horizon.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_peer(log_price: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Equal-weight leave-one-out industry log-price basket."""
    valid = log_price.notna().astype(float)
    group_sum = log_price.fillna(0.0).T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    group_count = valid.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    peer_count = group_count - valid
    peer = (group_sum - log_price.fillna(0.0)) / peer_count.where(peer_count >= 2.0)
    return peer, peer_count


def _rolling_level_hedge(
    y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Trailing OLS y=c+b*x, lagged one bar before use in the live spread."""
    valid = y.notna() & x.notna()
    yy = y.where(valid)
    xx = x.where(valid)
    min_obs = int(window * 0.8)

    mean_y = yy.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mean_x = xx.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    cov_yx = (yy * xx).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean() - mean_y * mean_x
    var_x = (xx * xx).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean() - mean_x * mean_x
    beta = cov_yx / var_x.where(var_x > 1e-10)
    intercept = mean_y - beta * mean_x

    return beta.shift(1), intercept.shift(1)


def _rolling_ar1(
    spread: pd.DataFrame, window: int, offset: int
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal AR(1) coefficient for spread[t]=c+phi*spread[t-1].

    Positive offsets select earlier non-overlapping trailing subsamples.
    """
    current = spread.shift(offset)
    lagged = spread.shift(offset + 1)
    valid = current.notna() & lagged.notna()
    current = current.where(valid)
    lagged = lagged.where(valid)
    min_obs = int(window * 0.8)

    mean_current = current.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mean_lagged = lagged.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    covariance = (
        (current * lagged).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
        - mean_current * mean_lagged
    )
    variance = (
        (lagged * lagged).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
        - mean_lagged * mean_lagged
    )
    phi = covariance / variance.where(variance > 1e-12)
    observations = valid.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).sum()
    return phi, observations


def _fast_stability_gate(
    phi0: pd.DataFrame,
    obs0: pd.DataFrame,
    phi1: pd.DataFrame,
    obs1: pd.DataFrame,
    phi2: pd.DataFrame,
    obs2: pd.DataFrame,
    beta: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Continuous quality score for stable 2--6 bar half-life relationships."""
    phi_stack = np.stack([phi0.to_numpy(), phi1.to_numpy(), phi2.to_numpy()], axis=0)
    obs_stack = np.stack([obs0.to_numpy(), obs1.to_numpy(), obs2.to_numpy()], axis=0)

    finite = np.all(np.isfinite(phi_stack), axis=0)
    fast = np.all((phi_stack >= 0.70) & (phi_stack <= 0.89), axis=0)
    enough = np.all(obs_stack >= 22.0, axis=0)
    phi_range = np.nanmax(phi_stack, axis=0) - np.nanmin(phi_stack, axis=0)

    beta_now = beta
    beta_mid = beta.shift(28)
    beta_old = beta.shift(56)
    beta_stack = np.stack(
        [beta_now.to_numpy(), beta_mid.to_numpy(), beta_old.to_numpy()], axis=0
    )
    beta_abs = np.abs(beta_stack)
    beta_finite = np.all(np.isfinite(beta_stack), axis=0)
    beta_size_ok = np.all((beta_abs >= 0.20) & (beta_abs <= 3.0), axis=0)
    beta_same_sign = (
        (np.sign(beta_stack[0]) == np.sign(beta_stack[1]))
        & (np.sign(beta_stack[1]) == np.sign(beta_stack[2]))
        & (np.sign(beta_stack[0]) != 0.0)
    )
    beta_ratio = np.nanmax(beta_abs, axis=0) / np.nanmin(beta_abs, axis=0)
    beta_stable = beta_ratio <= 1.5

    accepted = (
        finite
        & fast
        & enough
        & (phi_range <= 0.14)
        & beta_finite
        & beta_size_ok
        & beta_same_sign
        & beta_stable
    )
    quality = np.exp(-phi_range / 0.07) * np.exp(-np.log(beta_ratio) / 0.30)
    quality = np.where(accepted & np.isfinite(quality), quality, 0.0)
    return pd.DataFrame(quality, index=phi0.index, columns=phi0.columns)


@register_factor
class FastHalflifePeerSpreadRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "fast_halflife_peer_spread_repair"
    name = "Fast-Half-Life Peer Spread Repair"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Fades standardized leave-one-out industry spread residuals only when "
        "lagged hedge ratios and direct residual AR(1) half-lives are stable "
        "across causal trailing subsamples and imply repair within six bars."
    )
    window_length = 112
    inputs = ["close", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry = data["industry"]
        log_price = np.log(close.where(close > 0.0))

        labels = industry.iloc[0].astype(object).copy()
        missing = labels.isna()
        if missing.any():
            labels.loc[missing] = labels.index[missing]

        peer, peer_count = _leave_one_out_peer(log_price, labels)
        y = log_price.where(peer_count >= 2.0)
        x = peer.where(peer_count >= 2.0)

        beta, intercept = _rolling_level_hedge(y, x, 80)
        spread = y - intercept - beta * x

        phi0, obs0 = _rolling_ar1(spread, 28, 0)
        phi1, obs1 = _rolling_ar1(spread, 28, 28)
        phi2, obs2 = _rolling_ar1(spread, 28, 56)
        quality = _fast_stability_gate(phi0, obs0, phi1, obs1, phi2, obs2, beta)

        prior_mean = spread.rolling(30, min_periods=24).mean().shift(1)
        prior_std = spread.rolling(30, min_periods=24).std().shift(1)
        z_score = (spread - prior_mean) / prior_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        live_ok = (
            (phi0 >= 0.70)
            & (phi0 <= 0.89)
            & (obs0 >= 22.0)
            & (peer_count >= 2.0)
            & beta.notna()
        )
        signal = (-z_score.clip(-4.0, 4.0) * quality).where(live_ok, 0.0)
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Fast-Half-Life Peer Spread Repair
programs.trading_idea: Same-industry relative-price dislocations should revert over the six-bar forecast interval only when the peer spread has a demonstrably short and stable mean-reversion half-life. The prior implementation admitted slow error-correction relationships whose repair is more visible at longer horizons, diluting or reversing the six-bar effect. This refinement estimates the spread directly using a lagged rolling peer hedge, requires stable hedge ratios and AR(1) half-lives concentrated within roughly two to six bars, and trades the residual in its predicted convergence direction.
programs.description: Constructs a leave-one-out industry peer basket, estimates a causal rolling log-price hedge, and standardizes the resulting residual against its prior history. The signal fades extreme residuals only when direct residual AR(1) estimates and hedge weights are stable across three non-overlapping trailing subsamples and imply fast convergence.

programs.code:
"""Stable-peer copula rank discordance.

Mechanism: among persistently correlated sector peers, cash-generation quality and
relative price performance should have broadly concordant local empirical-copula
positions. Quality leaders that lag their stable peers, and weak-quality names
that lead them, represent valuation-quality discordances that should repair.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_demean(values: pd.DataFrame, sectors: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally remove the same-day sector component from a panel."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(sectors):
        positions = np.flatnonzero(sectors == label)
        if len(positions) == 0:
            continue
        block = values.iloc[:, positions]
        output.iloc[:, positions] = block.sub(block.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    return output


def _stable_peer_sets(
    residual_returns: pd.DataFrame,
    sectors: np.ndarray,
    lookback: int = 84,
    rebalance: int = 5,
    peers: int = 6,
    minimum_corr: float = 0.25,
) -> list[list[np.ndarray | None]]:
    """Create causal, sector-local peer sets stable across two refreshes.

    A peer is usable only if it is among the strongest correlations at both the
    current and preceding refresh. This intersection avoids transitive graph
    components, whose members need not themselves be close peers.
    """
    n_dates, n_assets = residual_returns.shape
    output: list[list[np.ndarray | None]] = [
        [None for _ in range(n_assets)] for _ in range(n_dates)
    ]
    previous = [set() for _ in range(n_assets)]
    active: list[np.ndarray | None] = [None for _ in range(n_assets)]

    for t in range(n_dates):
        if t < lookback - 1:
            continue

        if (t - (lookback - 1)) % rebalance == 0:
            current = [set() for _ in range(n_assets)]
            start = t - lookback + 1

            for label in pd.unique(sectors):
                positions = np.flatnonzero(sectors == label)
                if len(positions) < 5:
                    continue
                block = residual_returns.iloc[start : t + 1, positions]
                corr = block.corr(min_periods=lookback // 2).to_numpy(dtype=float)

                for local_i, global_i in enumerate(positions):
                    row = corr[local_i].copy()
                    row[local_i] = np.nan
                    candidates = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(row) & (row >= minimum_corr))
                    if len(candidates) == 0:
                        continue
                    ordered = candidates[np.argsort(row[candidates])[::-1]]
                    selected = positions[ordered[:peers]]
                    current[int(global_i)] = set(selected.astype(int).tolist())

            active = [None for _ in range(n_assets)]
            for i in range(n_assets):
                old = previous[i]
                new = current[i]
                if not old or not new:
                    continue
                overlap = len(old & new) / len(old | new)
                retained = sorted(old & new)
                if overlap >= 0.50 and len(retained) >= 3:
                    active[i] = np.asarray(retained, dtype=int)
            previous = current

        output[t] = active.copy()

    return output


def _local_rank_discordance(
    relative_return: pd.DataFrame,
    quality: pd.DataFrame,
    peer_sets: list[list[np.ndarray | None]],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return local quality-rank minus return-rank for stable peer baskets."""
    n_dates, n_assets = relative_return.shape
    result = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=relative_return.index, columns=relative_return.columns)

    for t in range(n_dates):
        for i in range(n_assets):
            peers = peer_sets[t][i]
            if peers is None:
                continue
            members = np.concatenate(([i], peers))
            q = quality.iloc[t, members].to_numpy(dtype=float)
            r = relative_return.iloc[t, members].to_numpy(dtype=float)
            valid = np.isfinite(q) & np.isfinite(r)
            if valid.sum() < 4 or not valid[0]:
                continue

            q_rank = pd.Series(q[valid]).rank(pct=True, method="average").to_numpy()
            r_rank = pd.Series(r[valid]).rank(pct=True, method="average").to_numpy()
            focal = int(np.flatnonzero(np.flatnonzero(valid) == 0)[0])
            gap = q_rank[focal] - r_rank[focal]

            # A small rank difference is ordinary basket noise rather than a tail event.
            if abs(gap) > 0.20:
                result.iat[t, i] = np.sign(gap) * (abs(gap) - 0.20)

    return result


@register_factor
class StablePeerCopulaRankDiscordance(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "stable_peer_copula_rank_discordance"
    name = "Stable Peer Copula Rank Discordance"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Ranks quality-minus-return copula discordance within sector-local peer "
        "sets whose residual-return correlations persist across consecutive refreshes."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "incomeQuality",
        "cashConversionCycle",
        "roic",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        daily_return = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        return_12 = close.pct_change(12, fill_method=None)

        sector_values = (
            data["sector"].ffill().iloc[-1].fillna("Unknown").astype(str).to_numpy()
        )
        residual_daily_return = _sector_demean(daily_return, sector_values)
        relative_return = _sector_demean(return_12, sector_values)

        fcf_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"].clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"].clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        roic = data["roic"].clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        cash_cycle_change = data["cashConversionCycle"].diff(63).clip(-365.0, 365.0)

        parts = [
            fcf_yield.rank(axis=1, pct=True),
            income_quality.rank(axis=1, pct=True),
            roic.rank(axis=1, pct=True),
            (-cash_cycle_change).rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        ]
        quality_sum = sum(part.fillna(0.0) for part in parts)
        quality_count = sum(part.notna().astype(float) for part in parts)
        quality = quality_sum / quality_count.where(quality_count >= 2)

        peers = _stable_peer_sets(residual_daily_return, sector_values)
        discordance = _local_rank_discordance(relative_return, quality, peers)
        active = discordance.ne(0.0)
        scored = rank(discordance.where(active)) - 0.5
        return scored.where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Stable Peer Copula Rank Discordance
programs.trading_idea: Within persistently correlated, sector-local peer relationships, price performance and cash-generation quality should occupy broadly concordant positions in the local empirical copula. A high-quality stock that is an unusually poor recent performer versus its stable peers is a catch-up candidate, while a weak-quality stock with an unusually strong peer-relative return is a fade candidate. Using only peer links that survive consecutive correlation refreshes concentrates the signal on economically coherent baskets and avoids treating transient correlation clusters as valuation anchors.
programs.description: Builds sector-local peer baskets from trailing correlations of sector-residual daily returns, retaining only peers present in consecutive refreshes. Within each stable basket it computes the difference between the quality rank and 12-day sector-relative-return rank, then retains only meaningful copula-rank discordances.

programs.code:
"""Coherent square-root impact overshoot from sparse-book displacement.

Mechanism: a large, close-confirmed directional move for modest participation
indicates that trading crossed unusually little displayed liquidity.  At daily
frequency the evidence supports interpreting these extreme impact episodes as
transient sparse-book pressure rather than permanent information discovery, so
positive efficient buying pressure is faded and negative pressure is bought.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _coherent_sqrt_impact(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robust excess impact under a square-root participation law."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    previous_close = safe_close.shift(1)
    log_return = np.log(safe_close / previous_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    dollar_volume = (safe_close * volume.where(volume > 0.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    typical_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(21, min_periods=12).median()
    relative_participation = dollar_volume / typical_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    relative_participation = relative_participation.clip(lower=0.25, upper=4.0)

    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    direction_confirmed = (np.sign(log_return) * close_location) >= 0.25

    realized_volatility = log_return.rolling(21, min_periods=12).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    efficient_impact = log_return / (
        realized_volatility * np.sqrt(relative_participation)
    )
    efficient_impact = efficient_impact.where(direction_confirmed)

    coherent_burst = efficient_impact.rolling(3, min_periods=2).mean()
    baseline = coherent_burst.rolling(63, min_periods=32).median()
    residual = coherent_burst - baseline
    mad = residual.abs().rolling(63, min_periods=32).median()
    robust_scale = (1.4826 * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    return (residual / robust_scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class CoherentSqrtImpactOvershoot(BaseFactor):
    """Industry-neutral robust sparse-book impact overshoot."""

    factor_id = "coherent_sqrt_impact_overshoot"
    name = "Coherent Square-Root Impact Overshoot"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Industry-neutral rank of a robust surprise in close-confirmed signed "
        "return per square root of relative dollar participation; high values "
        "represent positive sparse-book overshoots expected to reverse."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        impact_surprise = _coherent_sqrt_impact(
            close,
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["volume"],
        )
        neutral_surprise = indneutralize(
            impact_surprise.clip(-8.0, 8.0),
            data["industry"],
        )
        signal = rank(neutral_surprise)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.5).astype(float)
programs.name: Coherent Square-Root Impact Overshoot
programs.trading_idea: Large directional displacement for modest observed participation is the daily-bar footprint of a sparse order book: price traverses multiple liquidity levels before enough opposing liquidity appears. The original continuation interpretation is not supported by the out-of-sample evidence; instead, once direction is confirmed by the bar close, unusually efficient displacement appears to be predominantly transient liquidity-vacuum pressure and subsequently mean-reverts. A square-root participation normalization is more consistent with the empirical concavity of market impact and avoids the unstable division by a near-zero signed direction proxy.
programs.description: Computes a volatility-scaled signed return per square root of relative dollar participation, retaining only bars whose close location confirms the return direction. A short coherent burst is measured relative to its trailing robust median and MAD, neutralized by industry, and ranked cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Persistent uncertainty-shock beta, active only in building rough-volatility regimes.

Mechanism: persistent market-wide volatility increases induce mechanical deleveraging
by volatility-targeting, margin-sensitive, and risk-budget constrained investors. Stocks
whose returns have historically loaded negatively on volatility shocks are relatively
defensive, while positive uncertainty-beta names face incremental selling pressure.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fractional_filter(
    innovation: pd.Series,
    kernel_window: int = 45,
    memory_d: float = 0.30,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal normalized fractional filter with hyperbolically decaying memory."""
    weights = np.empty(kernel_window, dtype=float)
    weights[0] = 1.0
    for lag in range(1, kernel_window):
        weights[lag] = weights[lag - 1] * (lag - 1 + memory_d) / lag

    numerator = pd.Series(0.0, index=innovation.index, dtype=float)
    denominator = pd.Series(0.0, index=innovation.index, dtype=float)
    valid = innovation.notna().astype(float)

    for lag, weight in enumerate(weights):
        numerator = numerator + weight * innovation.shift(lag).fillna(0.0)
        denominator = denominator + weight * valid.shift(lag).fillna(0.0)

    required_weight = weights[:20].sum()
    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
        denominator >= required_weight
    )


def _orthogonalize_to_market(
    shock: pd.Series,
    market_return: pd.Series,
    window: int,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Remove trailing linear market-return exposure from a volatility innovation."""
    covariance = shock.rolling(window, min_periods=window).cov(market_return)
    variance = market_return.rolling(window, min_periods=window).var()
    beta = covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return shock - beta * market_return


def _rolling_shock_beta(
    stock_returns: pd.DataFrame,
    shock: pd.Series,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing OLS beta of each stock return to a common shock."""
    shock_panel = pd.DataFrame(
        np.repeat(shock.to_numpy()[:, None], stock_returns.shape[1], axis=1),
        index=stock_returns.index,
        columns=stock_returns.columns,
    )
    covariance = stock_returns.rolling(window, min_periods=window).cov(shock_panel)
    variance = shock_panel.rolling(window, min_periods=window).var()
    return covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _remove_size_exposure(signal: pd.DataFrame, market_cap: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Residualize a daily cross-section against log market capitalization."""
    log_cap = np.log(market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0))
    valid = signal.notna() & log_cap.notna()

    x = log_cap.where(valid)
    y = signal.where(valid)
    x_mean = x.mean(axis=1)
    y_mean = y.mean(axis=1)
    x_centered = x.sub(x_mean, axis=0)
    y_centered = y.sub(y_mean, axis=0)

    slope = (x_centered * y_centered).sum(axis=1) / x_centered.pow(2).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    residual = signal - x_centered.mul(slope, axis=0)
    return residual.where(valid, signal)


@register_factor
class OrthogonalRoughVolatilityBetaGate(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "orthogonal_rough_volatility_beta_gate"
    name = "Orthogonal Rough-Volatility Deleveraging Gate"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Negative beta to a market-return-orthogonalized persistent common range-volatility "
        "shock, sector- and size-neutralized and activated only during elevated, building stress."
    )
    window_length = 130
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "sector", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]

        safe_ratio = (high.abs() / low.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            (high.abs() > 0.0) & (low.abs() > 0.0)
        )
        log_range = np.log(safe_ratio).abs()
        range_variance = log_range.pow(2)

        # Median aggregation suppresses single-name jumps, halts, and bad bars.
        common_variance = range_variance.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
        common_logvol = np.log(common_variance.where(common_variance > 0.0))
        baseline = common_logvol.rolling(25, min_periods=20).median()
        innovation = common_logvol - baseline
        persistent = _fractional_filter(innovation)

        stock_returns = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        market_return = stock_returns.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
        orthogonal_shock = _orthogonalize_to_market(persistent, market_return, 60)
        shock_beta = _rolling_shock_beta(stock_returns, orthogonal_shock, 80)

        sectors = data["sector"].fillna("Unknown")
        exposure = indneutralize(-shock_beta, sectors)
        exposure = _remove_size_exposure(exposure, data["marketCap"])
        exposure_rank = rank(exposure).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.5)

        # A smooth state gate avoids a one-day spike and explicitly turns the
        # factor off outside a sustained, strengthening uncertainty episode.
        innovation_scale = innovation.rolling(80, min_periods=40).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        persistent_z = persistent / innovation_scale
        acceleration = persistent - persistent.shift(5)
        acceleration_z = acceleration / innovation_scale

        elevated = ((persistent_z - 0.50) / 1.50).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        building = (1.0 + acceleration_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)).fillna(0.0)
        gate = (elevated * building).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        return (0.5 + exposure_rank.sub(0.5).mul(gate, axis=0)).fillna(0.5)

The refined implementation separates the common volatility innovation from the contemporaneous market return, so the exposure is less likely to be a disguised equity-market beta. It activates the cross-section only when a robust, long-memory volatility state is both elevated and still strengthening, preserving the original mechanism as a timing and conditioning signal rather than treating every range fluctuation as a deleveraging episode.

"""Emergent structured execution with nonlinear impact predicts directional drift.

Mechanism: a fresh decline in the entropy of signed return/participation
transitions indicates that trading has become schedule-like, consistent with a
concealed metaorder.  When that structure coincides with unexpectedly high
range per square-root participation, latent liquidity is scarce and the
inferred order-flow direction should continue over the next several bars.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _execution_states(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return causal four-state signed-participation labels and relative volume."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close.pct_change()
    vol_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=12).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    rel_volume = volume / vol_base

    direction = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(ret >= 0.0, 1.0, 0.0), index=close.index, columns=close.columns
    )
    active = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(rel_volume >= 1.0, 1.0, 0.0), index=close.index, columns=close.columns
    )
    valid = ret.notna() & rel_volume.notna() & (volume > 0.0)
    states = (2.0 * direction + active).where(valid)
    return states, rel_volume


def _markov_entropy(states: pd.DataFrame, window: int, min_obs: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Smoothed, properly weighted conditional entropy of four causal states."""
    n_states = 4
    alpha = 0.5
    previous = states.shift(1)
    valid = previous.notna() & states.notna()
    observations = valid.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)

    for prior in range(n_states):
        counts = []
        row_total = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)
        for nxt in range(n_states):
            event = ((previous == float(prior)) & (states == float(nxt)) & valid).astype(float)
            count = event.rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum()
            counts.append(count)
            row_total = row_total + count

        row_weight = row_total / observations.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        denom = row_total + alpha * float(n_states)
        row_entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)
        for count in counts:
            probability = (count + alpha) / denom
            row_entropy = row_entropy - probability * np.log(probability)
        entropy = entropy + row_weight.fillna(0.0) * row_entropy

    return (entropy / np.log(float(n_states))).where(observations >= float(min_obs))


@register_factor
class AdaptiveMarkovExecutionImpactDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "adaptive_markov_execution_impact_drift"
    name = "Adaptive Markov Execution Impact Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Industry-neutral directional execution signal based on a fresh fall in "
        "return-volume transition entropy, persistent signed participation, and "
        "an unexpected nonlinear price-impact shock."
    )
    window_length = 100
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        states, rel_volume = _execution_states(close, volume)
        entropy = _markov_entropy(states, 36, 24)
        entropy_base = entropy.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=30).mean()
        entropy_scale = entropy.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=30).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        novelty = ((entropy_base - entropy) / entropy_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0) / 3.0

        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        ret = safe_close.pct_change()
        participation_weight = np.sqrt(rel_volume.clip(lower=0.05, upper=8.0))
        signed_pressure = (np.sign(ret) * participation_weight).rolling(6, min_periods=4).sum()
        total_pressure = participation_weight.rolling(6, min_periods=4).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        direction = (signed_pressure / total_pressure).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        persistent_direction = direction * direction.abs()

        range_fraction = (high - low).abs() / safe_close
        impact = range_fraction / np.sqrt(rel_volume.clip(lower=0.05, upper=20.0))
        log_impact = np.log(impact.where(impact > 0.0))
        impact_base = log_impact.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=20).median()
        impact_surge = (log_impact - impact_base).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0) / 2.0

        raw = persistent_direction * novelty * impact_surge
        neutral = indneutralize(raw.fillna(0.0), data["industry"])
        signal = rank(neutral)
        return signal.where(raw.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A newly persistent, low-entropy sequence of signed return and participation states is a daily-bar proxy for an emerging concealed execution program rather than ordinary independent trading noise. Unlike the prior magnitude-only implementation, the signed state sequence identifies the likely metaorder side, while an unexpected increase in square-root-law price impact indicates that latent liquidity is thin enough for the order flow to continue moving prices. The signal is industry-neutralized so it targets idiosyncratic execution pressure rather than broad sector momentum.

"""Event-marked peer-excitation completion factor.

Mechanism: a fresh positive earnings event makes a stock temporarily susceptible to
industry-level buy-flow clustering.  When peer signed-flow excitation arrives but
the target has not yet matched it in industry-relative returns, the remaining
response is expected to complete over the following trading week.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional leave-one-out mean for each static industry."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    aligned = labels.reindex(values.columns).fillna("Unknown")
    for group in pd.unique(aligned):
        members = aligned.index[aligned == group]
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        block = values.loc[:, members]
        total = block.sum(axis=1).to_numpy()[:, None]
        out.loc[:, members] = (total - block.to_numpy()) / float(len(members) - 1)
    return out


def _fresh_change(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Retain a quarterly field only when a newly available value is observed."""
    clean = value.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    changed = clean.notna() & clean.ne(clean.shift(1))
    return clean.where(changed, 0.0).fillna(0.0)


def _decayed_impulse(impulse: pd.DataFrame, length: int, half_life: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Finite causal exponential kernel applied to event impulses."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=impulse.index, columns=impulse.columns)
    for lag in range(length):
        weight = float(np.exp(-np.log(2.0) * lag / half_life))
        out = out + weight * impulse.shift(lag).fillna(0.0)
    return out


@register_factor
class EventMarkedPeerExcitationCompletion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "event_marked_peer_excitation_completion"
    name = "Event-Marked Peer Excitation Completion"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Ranks recently positive-surprised, attention-prone stocks with lagged "
        "industry peer buy-flow excitation that exceeds their realized "
        "industry-relative response."
    )
    window_length = 100
    inputs = [
        "close", "high", "low", "volume", "industry", "marketCap",
        "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise"
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace(0.0, np.nan)

        labels = data["industry"].ffill().iloc[-1].reindex(close.columns).fillna("Unknown")
        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        peer_ret = _leave_one_out_mean(ret, labels)
        idio_ret = ret - peer_ret
        idio_vol = idio_ret.rolling(30, min_periods=15).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        realized_response = (idio_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=2).sum() / idio_vol).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)

        eps_raw = data["epsSurprise"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        rev_raw = data["revenueSurprise"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_event = _fresh_change(eps_raw)
        rev_event = _fresh_change(rev_raw)
        eps_scale = eps_raw.abs().rolling(252, min_periods=20).median().shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rev_scale = rev_raw.abs().rolling(252, min_periods=20).median().shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eps_z = (eps_event / eps_scale).clip(-6.0, 6.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        rev_z = (rev_event / rev_scale).clip(-6.0, 6.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        positive_event = (0.7 * eps_z + 0.3 * rev_z).clip(lower=0.0)

        relative_volume = volume / volume.rolling(40, min_periods=15).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_volume = relative_volume.clip(0.0, 8.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        small_cap = 1.0 - rank(np.log1p(market_cap.clip(lower=0.0)))
        attention = (0.65 * small_cap.fillna(0.5) + 0.35 * rank(relative_volume).fillna(0.5)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        event_mark = (positive_event * (0.4 + 0.6 * attention)).clip(0.0, 6.0)
        susceptibility = _decayed_impulse(event_mark, 6, 2.5).clip(0.0, 10.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        flow = close_location * np.sqrt(relative_volume.fillna(0.0))
        flow_mean = flow.rolling(60, min_periods=25).mean()
        flow_std = flow.rolling(60, min_periods=25).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        normalized_flow = ((flow - flow_mean) / flow_std).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)
        peer_buy = _leave_one_out_mean(normalized_flow, labels).clip(lower=0.0)
        peer_excitation = _decayed_impulse(peer_buy.shift(1).fillna(0.0), 5, 1.8)
        excitation_mean = peer_excitation.rolling(60, min_periods=25).mean()
        excitation_std = peer_excitation.rolling(60, min_periods=25).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        excitation_z = ((peer_excitation - excitation_mean) / excitation_std).clip(-3.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)

        unpaid_excitation = (excitation_z - realized_response).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        signal = (susceptibility * unpaid_excitation).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(signal).fillna(0.5)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _volume_anchor(
    typical_price: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    halflife: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially weighted, volume-weighted reference price."""
    valid_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0, np.nan)
    numerator = (typical_price * valid_volume).ewm(
        halflife=halflife, adjust=False, min_periods=1
    ).mean()
    denominator = valid_volume.ewm(
        halflife=halflife, adjust=False, min_periods=1
    ).mean()
    return numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _absorbed_sell_rebound_score(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Find underwater names where coherent selling is being absorbed."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    safe_volume = volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    typical = ((high + low + safe_close) / 3.0).where(safe_close.notna())
    fast_anchor = _volume_anchor(typical, safe_volume, 12)
    slow_anchor = _volume_anchor(typical, safe_volume, 50)

    fast_gap = ((fast_anchor - safe_close) / fast_anchor.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)
    slow_gap = ((slow_anchor - safe_close) / slow_anchor.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)
    underwater = (fast_gap.fillna(0.0) + slow_gap.fillna(0.0)) / 2.0

    close_location_signed = (
        (2.0 * safe_close - high - low) / bar_range
    ).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
    signed_flow = close_location_signed * safe_volume
    flow_window = 8
    pressure = signed_flow.rolling(flow_window, min_periods=flow_window).sum() / safe_volume.rolling(
        flow_window, min_periods=flow_window
    ).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    displacement = safe_close / safe_close.shift(flow_window) - 1.0
    path_length = safe_close.pct_change().abs().rolling(
        flow_window, min_periods=flow_window
    ).sum()
    aligned_move = (np.sign(pressure) * displacement).clip(lower=0.0)
    efficiency = aligned_move / path_length.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    low_efficiency = 1.0 - ts_rank(efficiency, 35)

    absorbed_selling = (-pressure).clip(lower=0.0) * low_efficiency.fillna(0.0)
    rebound_confirmation = ((safe_close - low) / bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.5)
    score = underwater * absorbed_selling * rebound_confirmation
    return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class UnderwaterAbsorbedSellRebound(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "underwater_absorbed_sell_rebound"
    name = "Underwater Absorbed-Sell Rebound"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Ranks stocks below fast and slow volume-weighted cost-basis anchors "
        "when persistent negative flow has low price efficiency and the bar closes strongly."
    )
    window_length = 50
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        score = _absorbed_sell_rebound_score(
            data["close"].astype(float),
            data["high"].astype(float),
            data["low"].astype(float),
            data["volume"].astype(float),
        )
        return rank(score).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.5)

This combines loss-aversion support from underwater cohorts with the microstructural evidence that liquidity providers are absorbing, rather than clearing, continuing sell pressure. Neither parent alone distinguishes a generic below-anchor rebound from a sell-flow episode that is demonstrably being absorbed; the interaction identifies liquidation whose marginal supply is becoming exhausted while latent demand remains.
