"""Seasoned convexity-wedge liquidity residual fade.

Mechanism: sector-relative price shocks are more likely to repair when unusually
large intrabar variance is created in thin trading without surviving as
close-to-close variance.  Near a seasoned price anchor, this is consistent with
temporary variance-hedging and quote-withdrawal pressure rather than durable
information discovery, so the signal fades the residual displacement.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_sector_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Same-bar leave-one-out sector return and available peer count."""
    benchmark = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    for group in pd.unique(sector.to_numpy().ravel()):
        if not pd.notna(group):
            continue
        members = sector.eq(group)
        group_ret = ret.where(members)
        total = group_ret.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        count = group_ret.notna().sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        loo = ret.rsub(total, axis=0).div((count - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        benchmark = benchmark.where(~members, loo)
        count_frame = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(count.to_numpy()[:, None], ret.shape[1], axis=1),
            index=ret.index,
            columns=ret.columns,
        )
        peer_count = peer_count.where(~members, count_frame)

    return benchmark, peer_count


def _robust_zscore(df: pd.DataFrame, window: int, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing median/MAD z-score, robust to the shock being measured."""
    median = df.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).median()
    mad = df.sub(median).abs().rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).median()
    scale = (1.4826 * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return df.sub(median).div(scale)


def _convexity_anchor_state(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal intrabar convexity wedge times seasoned zero-vanna-style anchor.

    Garman-Klass variance isolates intrabar movement more cleanly than a raw
    high-low range.  Its excess over close-to-close realized variance identifies
    movement that did not persist into the closing mark.
    """
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    safe_open = open_.where(open_ > 0.0)
    safe_high = high.where(high > 0.0)
    safe_low = low.where(low > 0.0)

    log_price = np.log(safe_close)
    log_return = log_price.diff()
    hl = np.log(safe_high.div(safe_low))
    oc = np.log(safe_close.div(safe_open))

    gk_variance = (
        0.5 * hl.pow(2) - (2.0 * np.log(2.0) - 1.0) * oc.pow(2)
    ).clip(lower=0.0)
    close_variance = log_return.pow(2)

    intrabar_var = gk_variance.rolling(15, min_periods=10).mean()
    close_var = close_variance.rolling(15, min_periods=10).mean()
    wedge = np.log((intrabar_var + 1e-10).div(close_var + 1e-10))
    wedge_z = _robust_zscore(wedge, 84, 42).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
    wedge_state = wedge_z.div(1.0 + wedge_z)

    seasoned_center = log_price.rolling(63, min_periods=40).mean()
    seasoned_vol = log_return.rolling(63, min_periods=40).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    distance = log_price.sub(seasoned_center).div(seasoned_vol * np.sqrt(63.0))
    anchor = np.exp(-0.5 * distance.clip(lower=-4.0, upper=4.0).pow(2))

    return wedge_state.mul(anchor)


@register_factor
class SeasonedConvexityWedgeLiquidityResidualFade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "seasoned_convexity_wedge_liquidity_residual_fade"
    name = "Seasoned Convexity-Wedge Liquidity Fade"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fades robust sector-residual shocks when Garman-Klass intrabar variance "
        "is unusually high relative to close variance, dollar-volume is thin, and "
        "spot remains near its seasoned anchor."
    )
    window_length = 100
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = close.div(prior_close).sub(1.0)
        sector_ret, breadth = _leave_one_out_sector_return(ret, data["sector"])
        residual = ret.sub(sector_ret)

        residual_z = _robust_zscore(residual, 42, 25).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)

        dollar_volume = close.abs().mul(volume).where(lambda x: x > 0.0)
        log_dollar_volume = np.log(dollar_volume)
        thin_z = (-_robust_zscore(log_dollar_volume, 63, 35)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
        thin_state = thin_z.div(1.0 + thin_z)

        convexity_anchor = _convexity_anchor_state(close, open_, high, low)
        state = np.sqrt(thin_state.mul(convexity_anchor)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        raw = -residual_z.mul(state)
        active = (
            (breadth >= 4.0)
            & residual_z.notna()
            & state.notna()
            & (state > 0.05)
        )
        signal = rank(raw.where(active)).sub(0.5)
        return signal.where(active, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Seasoned Convexity-Wedge Liquidity Fade
programs.trading_idea: A large sector-relative return should reverse when it is accompanied by unusually high intrabar variance relative to close-to-close variance and occurs on unusually low dollar-volume participation. This combination is a cleaner daily-bar proxy for temporary convexity-hedging and quote-withdrawal pressure: substantial within-bar movement was created without commensurate closing-price discovery. The effect is concentrated when spot remains close to its seasoned log-price anchor, where zero-vanna-style hedge adjustments are more likely to be temporary rather than the start of a directional repricing.
programs.description: The signal fades robust sector-residual return shocks, weighted by a Garman-Klass versus close-variance wedge, relative dollar-volume thinness, and proximity to a seasoned price anchor. It requires sufficient leave-one-out sector peer breadth and ranks only active observations cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Complexity-gated underreaction to disclosed gross-margin efficiency changes.

Mechanism: earnings headlines are processed quickly, whereas translating a reported
cost-efficiency change into sustainable profitability requires more analysis for firms
with substantial R&D and organisational spending.  A margin innovation not explained
by the headline EPS surprise should therefore drift in its direction when the initial
industry-relative price response is incomplete.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_demean(values: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract same-date industry means without using future observations."""
    labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(values.columns).fillna("__unknown__")
    output = values.copy()
    for label in pd.unique(labels):
        cols = labels.index[labels == label]
        subset = values.loc[:, cols]
        output.loc[:, cols] = subset.sub(subset.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    return output


def _signed_cross_sectional_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Map a cross-section to [-1, 1], retaining missing observations as NaN."""
    return 2.0 * rank(values) - 1.0


def _cross_sectional_residual(
    target: pd.DataFrame, control: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date zero-intercept projection after group demeaning.

    The control is rank-bounded before this helper is called, limiting leverage from
    unusually scaled EPS surprises.  Each row uses only values public on that row.
    """
    valid = target.notna() & control.notna()
    x = control.where(valid, 0.0)
    y = target.where(valid, 0.0)
    denominator = (x * x).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = (x * y).sum(axis=1).div(denominator).fillna(0.0)
    residual = target - control.mul(beta, axis=0)
    return residual.where(target.notna())


def _finite_event_carry(
    events: pd.DataFrame, bars: int, half_life: float
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally retain a sparse report event for a finite post-report interval."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=events.index, columns=events.columns)
    decay = np.log(2.0) / half_life
    for lag in range(bars):
        result = result + events.shift(lag).fillna(0.0) * float(np.exp(-decay * lag))
    return result


@register_factor
class ComplexityGatedMarginAssimilationResidual(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "complexity_gated_margin_assimilation_residual"
    name = "Complexity-Gated Margin Assimilation Residual"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Ranks industry-relative gross-margin innovations after removing their "
        "contemporaneous EPS-surprise component, and longs or shorts only when "
        "the short initial price response has underreacted in the innovation's "
        "direction. Operational complexity from R&D and SG&A intensity amplifies "
        "the event signal."
    )
    window_length = 7
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "grossMargin",
        "rdToRevenue",
        "sgaToRevenue",
        "epsSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry = data["industry"]
        margin = data["grossMargin"]

        # Fundamental fields are point-in-time quarterly step functions. A change is
        # consequently the newly available report event, rather than a repeated daily
        # observation of the same accounting result.
        margin_change = margin - margin.shift(1)
        event = (
            margin.notna()
            & margin.shift(1).notna()
            & (margin_change.abs() > 1.0e-12)
        )
        raw_innovation = margin_change.where(event)
        industry_innovation = _industry_demean(raw_innovation, industry)

        # EPS-surprise ranks are bounded before residualisation, avoiding domination
        # by different EPS units or a small number of extreme surprise observations.
        surprise_at_event = data["epsSurprise"].where(event)
        surprise_score = _signed_cross_sectional_rank(surprise_at_event)
        industry_surprise = _industry_demean(surprise_score, industry)
        residual_innovation = _cross_sectional_residual(
            industry_innovation, industry_surprise
        )
        fundamental_score = _signed_cross_sectional_rank(residual_innovation)

        # A three-session reaction includes the report-day response while allowing for
        # filing-time variation. Industry demeaning removes broad peer repricing.
        reaction = close.div(close.shift(3).replace(0.0, np.nan)) - 1.0
        reaction_score = _signed_cross_sectional_rank(
            _industry_demean(reaction, industry)
        )

        # R&D and SG&A intensity proxy the analytical burden of separating durable
        # efficiency from transitory accounting noise. Relative complexity is used so
        # that structurally high-cost industries are not mechanically favoured.
        complexity = (
            data["rdToRevenue"].clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
            + data["sgaToRevenue"].clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        )
        relative_complexity = _industry_demean(np.log1p(complexity), industry)
        complexity_gate = rank(relative_complexity).fillna(0.0)

        recognition_residual = fundamental_score - reaction_score
        directional_underreaction = recognition_residual * fundamental_score > 0.0
        event_signal = (
            recognition_residual
            * complexity_gate
        ).where(event & directional_underreaction, 0.0)
        event_signal = event_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        carried = _finite_event_carry(event_signal, 7, 4.0)
        return rank(carried).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Complexity-Gated Margin Assimilation Residual
programs.trading_idea: Investors process headline earnings news quickly but can underweight the information in a newly disclosed change in gross-margin efficiency, especially when high R&D and SG&A intensity makes it harder to infer whether the cost change is durable. The signal isolates the industry-relative margin innovation not explained by the contemporaneous EPS surprise, then measures whether the stock's short report-window reaction has underreacted in the same direction. High-complexity firms with positive unassimilated margin news should outperform, while those with negative unassimilated margin news should underperform over the following six sessions.
programs.description: The factor detects newly available gross-margin changes, industry-demeans and residualizes them against ranked EPS surprises, and compares the resulting fundamental innovation with the contemporaneous industry-relative price response. Directionally underreacted events are weighted by industry-relative R&D plus SG&A intensity and carried forward with a short causal decay.

programs.code:
"""Mature self-exciting flow-cluster saturation reversal.

Mechanism: abnormal volume marked by the sign and magnitude of a daily return
is a coarse proxy for self-exciting directional order flow.  A range and volume
shock is treated as terminal price impact only when it follows an established
same-side cluster; excluding the current mark from the cluster state separates
mature inventory pressure from fresh potentially informative flow.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_exp_intensity(events: pd.DataFrame, half_life: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Exponentially decayed marked-event intensity known before each bar.

    At t the output contains only events through t-1, decayed once into t.
    This makes the state a measure of pre-existing cluster maturity rather
    than a mechanical transformation of the current return.
    """
    values = events.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    output = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=float)
    state = np.zeros(values.shape[1], dtype=float)
    decay = float(np.exp(-np.log(2.0) / half_life))

    for t in range(values.shape[0]):
        prior_state = decay * state
        output[t] = prior_state
        state = prior_state + values[t]

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=events.index, columns=events.columns)


@register_factor
class MatureClusterRangeSaturationReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "mature_cluster_range_saturation_reversal"
    name = "Mature Flow-Cluster Range Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral reversal score from a mature signed abnormal-volume "
        "cluster followed by a renewed abnormal-volume excess-range shock."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float).where(data["close"].astype(float) > 0.0)
        safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        high_raw = data["high"].astype(float)
        low_raw = data["low"].astype(float)
        high = high_raw.where(high_raw > 0.0, safe_close)
        low = low_raw.where(low_raw > 0.0, safe_close)
        upper = pd.DataFrame(
            np.maximum(high.to_numpy(dtype=float), low.to_numpy(dtype=float)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        lower = pd.DataFrame(
            np.minimum(high.to_numpy(dtype=float), low.to_numpy(dtype=float)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

        relative_range = ((upper - lower).clip(lower=0.0) / safe_close).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        range_measure = np.log1p(relative_range).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_range_level = range_measure.rolling(30, min_periods=20).median().shift(1)
        range_shock = np.log(range_measure / prior_range_level.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        range_shock = range_shock.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0).fillna(0.0)

        volume_raw = data["volume"].astype(float)
        volume = volume_raw.where(volume_raw > 0.0)
        prior_volume_level = volume.rolling(30, min_periods=20).median().shift(1)
        activity_shock = np.log(volume / prior_volume_level.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        activity_shock = activity_shock.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0).fillna(0.0)

        log_return = np.log(safe_close).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        prior_volatility = log_return.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
        standardized_move = np.tanh(log_return / prior_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        standardized_move = standardized_move.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        positive_marks = activity_shock * standardized_move.clip(lower=0.0)
        negative_marks = activity_shock * (-standardized_move.clip(upper=0.0))

        positive_state = _prior_exp_intensity(positive_marks, 5.0)
        negative_state = _prior_exp_intensity(negative_marks, 5.0)
        signed_state = positive_state - negative_state
        total_state = positive_state + negative_state

        prior_cluster_scale = total_state.rolling(60, min_periods=30).mean().shift(1)
        mature_direction = signed_state / prior_cluster_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        mature_direction = mature_direction.clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)

        raw_signal = -mature_direction * activity_shock * range_shock
        groups = data["sector"].fillna("Unknown")
        neutral_signal = indneutralize(raw_signal.fillna(0.0), groups)
        return rank(neutral_signal).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Mature Flow-Cluster Range Reversal
programs.trading_idea: Abnormal volume signed by standardized daily returns is a coarse proxy for marked self-exciting order flow. The refinement separates an established directional cluster from the current bar: only prior excitation is treated as inventory already accumulated, while a renewed abnormal-volume range expansion is interpreted as a late-stage impact payment rather than a fresh signal. The expected sign is positive because the returned score is explicitly the opposite of the mature cluster direction: prior sell clusters produce high positive rebound scores and prior buy clusters produce low scores; the prior version's sign contradiction was a signal-convention error, not evidence against the reversal mechanism.
programs.description: Computes exponentially decayed positive and negative abnormal-participation states excluding the current bar, normalizes their directional imbalance by recent cluster activity, and reverses that mature pressure only when the current bar has both abnormal volume and an excess realized range. The result is sector-neutralized and cross-sectionally ranked.

programs.code:
"""Habit-risk premium from downside semibeta and commitment rigidity.

Mechanism: broad losses raise habit-driven risk aversion. Claims with unusually
large loading on the market's downside component, particularly firms with less
flexible operating and financing commitments, require a higher expected return
when aggregate stress has just intensified.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _semibeta_asymmetry(
    stock_returns: pd.DataFrame, market_returns: pd.Series, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing downside-beta minus ordinary beta using all available days.

    The downside regressor is min(market return, 0), which avoids the small,
    discontinuously selected sample used by conditional downside regressions.
    All moments are trailing and therefore causal.
    """
    downside_market = market_returns.clip(upper=0.0)
    minimum = max(40, window // 2)

    mean_stock = stock_returns.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()
    mean_market = market_returns.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()
    mean_downside = downside_market.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()

    stock_market = stock_returns.mul(market_returns, axis=0).rolling(
        window, min_periods=minimum
    ).mean()
    stock_downside = stock_returns.mul(downside_market, axis=0).rolling(
        window, min_periods=minimum
    ).mean()
    market_sq = (market_returns * market_returns).rolling(
        window, min_periods=minimum
    ).mean()
    downside_sq = (downside_market * downside_market).rolling(
        window, min_periods=minimum
    ).mean()

    ordinary_covariance = stock_market.sub(mean_stock.mul(mean_market, axis=0))
    downside_covariance = stock_downside.sub(mean_stock.mul(mean_downside, axis=0))
    ordinary_variance = market_sq - mean_market * mean_market
    downside_variance = downside_sq - mean_downside * mean_downside

    ordinary_beta = ordinary_covariance.div(ordinary_variance.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
    downside_beta = downside_covariance.div(downside_variance.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
    return downside_beta - ordinary_beta


def _commitment_rank(
    sga_expense: pd.DataFrame,
    interest_expense: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust cross-sectional commitment score with neutral sparse-field treatment."""
    valid_revenue = revenue.where(revenue > 0.0)
    sga_ratio = sga_expense.where(sga_expense >= 0.0).div(valid_revenue)
    interest_ratio = interest_expense.where(interest_expense >= 0.0).div(valid_revenue)

    sga_rank = sga_ratio.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    interest_rank = interest_ratio.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    available = sga_rank.notna().astype(float) + interest_rank.notna().astype(float)
    combined = sga_rank.fillna(0.0) + interest_rank.fillna(0.0)
    commitment = combined.div(available.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    return commitment.fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class HabitSemibetaCommitmentStressPremium(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "habit_semibeta_commitment_stress_premium"
    name = "Habit Semibeta Commitment Premium"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Centered rank of downside-beta asymmetry and operating/financing "
        "commitment rigidity, scaled smoothly by a recent aggregate drawdown."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["close", "sgaExpense", "interestExpense", "revenue"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        stock_returns = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        market_returns = stock_returns.median(axis=1, skipna=True)

        beta_asymmetry = _semibeta_asymmetry(stock_returns, market_returns, 126)
        beta_rank = beta_asymmetry.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        commitment = _commitment_rank(
            data["sgaExpense"], data["interestExpense"], data["revenue"]
        )

        exposure = 0.5 * beta_rank + 0.5 * commitment
        centered_exposure = exposure - 0.5

        recent_market_loss = -market_returns.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        market_volatility = market_returns.rolling(63, min_periods=32).std()
        stress_intensity = recent_market_loss.div(
            market_volatility * np.sqrt(3.0)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        signal = centered_exposure.mul(stress_intensity.fillna(0.0), axis=0)
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Habit Semibeta Commitment Premium
programs.trading_idea: Habit-driven risk aversion rises after broad market losses, increasing the required return on claims whose payoffs co-move most with the market's downside component. The prior result's positive realized sign is consistent with this being an expected-return premium rather than an immediate further selloff: after a stress onset, investors demand higher compensation for high-downside-beta firms, especially where operating and financing commitments limit adjustment capacity. This refinement replaces sparse conditional-regression branches and thresholded gating with a stable semibeta asymmetry and a smooth, timely aggregate-loss intensity.
programs.description: Ranks stocks by trailing downside-beta asymmetry and by a neutral-filled commitment measure based on SG&A and interest expense relative to revenue. The centered exposure is scaled by the magnitude of a recent broad-market drawdown relative to trailing market volatility.

programs.code:
"""Fresh repricing of concentrated industry-tail exposure.

Mechanism: diversification fails at finite horizons when an industry's downside
is dominated by a few constituents rather than a broad common shock.  A fresh
concentrated downside episode reveals this non-diversified tail exposure, and
high conditional downside-beta, leveraged firms face near-term deleveraging
pressure.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _expand_group_values(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a group-level panel to constituent columns."""
    out = values.reindex(columns=list(labels.to_numpy()))
    out.columns = columns
    return out


def _tail_semibeta_and_freshness(ret: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causally estimate conditional downside beta and a short event clock."""
    valid = ret.notna().astype(float)
    group_sum = ret.fillna(0.0).T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum().T
    group_count = valid.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum().T
    sum_for_stock = _expand_group_values(group_sum, labels, ret.columns)
    count_for_stock = _expand_group_values(group_count, labels, ret.columns)

    loo_count = count_for_stock - valid
    loo_ret = (sum_for_stock - ret.fillna(0.0)) / loo_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    mean = loo_ret.rolling(80, min_periods=40).mean()
    tail_cutoff = loo_ret.rolling(80, min_periods=40).quantile(0.20)
    broad_downside = (loo_ret <= tail_cutoff) & (loo_ret < mean) & (loo_count >= 2.0)

    downside = (-ret).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
    group_downside = downside.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum().T
    group_downside_sq = (downside * downside).T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum().T
    hhi = group_downside_sq / group_downside.pow(2).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    n_group = group_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    normalized_hhi = (hhi - 1.0 / n_group) / (1.0 - 1.0 / n_group).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    normalized_hhi = normalized_hhi.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    concentration = _expand_group_values(normalized_hhi, labels, ret.columns)
    concentration_cutoff = concentration.rolling(60, min_periods=30).quantile(0.60)
    concentrated_event = (broad_downside & (concentration >= concentration_cutoff)).fillna(False)

    own_loss = (-ret).clip(lower=0.0).where(concentrated_event)
    peer_loss = (-loo_ret).clip(lower=0.0).where(concentrated_event)
    avg_own_loss = own_loss.rolling(50, min_periods=3).mean()
    avg_peer_loss = peer_loss.rolling(50, min_periods=3).mean()
    semibeta = (avg_own_loss / avg_peer_loss.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

    freshness = concentrated_event.astype(float).rolling(3, min_periods=1).max()
    return semibeta, freshness


@register_factor
class PenultimateTailSemibetaFreshnessReprice(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "penultimate_tail_semibeta_freshness_reprice"
    name = "Fresh Penultimate Tail Semibeta Reprice"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Negative rank of fresh concentrated-industry downside semibeta, "
        "amplified by balance-sheet leverage."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "industry", "sector", "debtToEquity"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        ret = close.pct_change()

        industry = data["industry"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        sector = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        labels = industry.iloc[0].copy()
        labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), sector.iloc[0])
        fallback = pd.Series(close.columns, index=close.columns, dtype=object)
        labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), fallback).astype(str)

        semibeta, freshness = _tail_semibeta_and_freshness(ret, labels)

        leverage = data["debtToEquity"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        leverage_rank = rank(leverage.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0))
        tail_risk = semibeta * (0.5 + leverage_rank) * freshness

        signal = rank(-tail_risk.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0))
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Fresh Penultimate Tail Semibeta Reprice
programs.trading_idea: Diversification failure should be priced most quickly immediately after a fresh, concentrated industry downside episode, rather than from a slowly accumulated and sparse co-crash-count statistic. Firms with large realized downside semibeta to these concentrated leave-one-out industry shocks have revealed exposure to non-diversified tail risk; leverage makes the subsequent risk-budget and deleveraging response more acute. The signal therefore shorts recently activated, tail-sensitive, leveraged firms and is neutral-to-long less exposed peers.
programs.description: The factor identifies concentrated leave-one-out industry downside events using an effective-number-adjusted downside HHI, estimates each stock's trailing conditional downside semibeta during those events, and activates the exposure only for several days after a fresh event. It ranks the negative of this fresh tail-risk exposure, with balance-sheet leverage as a severity multiplier.

programs.code:
"""Fresh cash-funded debt-service repair after quarterly disclosure.

Mechanism: a newly disclosed reduction in net debt is more credible when it is
paired with positive operating cash flow, improving margins, and no meaningful
equity dilution.  Complex balance-sheet repair can be incorporated gradually
when the initial sector-relative price response is muted.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile ranks within each sector, row by row."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    labels = pd.unique(sector.to_numpy().ravel())
    for label in labels:
        if pd.isna(label):
            continue
        members = sector.eq(label)
        ranked = rank(values.where(members))
        out = out.where(~members, ranked)
    return out


def _event_carry(event_signal: pd.DataFrame, bars: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Carry a report-date signal forward with a causal six-bar decay."""
    carried = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=event_signal.index, columns=event_signal.columns)
    for lag in range(bars):
        weight = float(np.exp(-lag / 2.5))
        carried = carried + weight * event_signal.shift(lag).fillna(0.0)
    return carried


@register_factor
class FreshCashDebtServiceRepairAssimilation(BaseFactor):
    """Fresh fundamental repair events whose initial price reaction is muted."""

    factor_id = "fresh_cash_debt_service_repair_assimilation"
    name = "Fresh Cash-Funded Debt-Service Repair"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Sector-relative rank of newly reported cash-funded deleveraging, margin "
        "improvement, debt-service capacity, and anti-dilution, retained briefly "
        "when the initial sector-relative return has not already recognized it."
    )
    window_length = 7
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "totalDebt",
        "cash",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "operatingMargin",
        "sharesOutstanding",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        total_debt = data["totalDebt"]
        cash = data["cash"]
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]
        free_cash_flow = data["freeCashFlow"]
        operating_margin = data["operatingMargin"]
        shares = data["sharesOutstanding"]

        net_debt = total_debt - cash
        prior_net_debt = net_debt.shift(1)
        prior_debt_scale = total_debt.shift(1).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        deleveraging = ((prior_net_debt - net_debt) / prior_debt_scale).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        margin_change = (operating_margin - operating_margin.shift(1)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        cash_debt_service = (operating_cash_flow / total_debt.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        anti_dilution = (1.0 - shares / shares.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        required = (
            total_debt.notna()
            & total_debt.shift(1).notna()
            & cash.notna()
            & cash.shift(1).notna()
            & operating_cash_flow.notna()
            & operating_margin.notna()
            & operating_margin.shift(1).notna()
            & shares.notna()
            & shares.shift(1).notna()
            & free_cash_flow.notna()
        )

        report_update = (
            operating_margin.ne(operating_margin.shift(1))
            | operating_cash_flow.ne(operating_cash_flow.shift(1))
            | total_debt.ne(total_debt.shift(1))
        ) & required

        debt_score = _sector_rank(deleveraging.where(report_update), sector)
        margin_score = _sector_rank(margin_change.where(report_update), sector)
        service_score = _sector_rank(cash_debt_service.where(report_update), sector)
        dilution_score = _sector_rank(anti_dilution.where(report_update), sector)

        joint_repair = (
            debt_score.fillna(0.0)
            * margin_score.fillna(0.0)
            * service_score.fillna(0.0)
            * dilution_score.fillna(0.0)
        ) ** 0.25

        one_day_return = close / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        response_rank = _sector_rank(one_day_return, sector)
        muted_response = response_rank.le(0.65) & response_rank.ge(0.10)

        cash_funded = operating_cash_flow.gt(0.0) & free_cash_flow.gt(0.0)
        event_signal = joint_repair.where(report_update & cash_funded & muted_response)
        carried = _event_carry(event_signal, 6)

        return _sector_rank(carried.where(carried.gt(0.0)), sector).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank


def _leave_one_out_cap_weighted_return(
    returns_frame: pd.DataFrame,
    sector_frame: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal leave-one-out sector basket return with defensive cap weighting."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=returns_frame.index, columns=returns_frame.columns)
    labels = sector_frame.iloc[0]

    for sector_name in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels.eq(sector_name)]
        if len(members) < 3:
            continue

        group_ret = returns_frame.loc[:, members]
        raw_cap = market_cap.loc[:, members]
        weights = raw_cap.where(raw_cap.gt(0.0), 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(1.0)
        valid = group_ret.notna()
        used_weight = weights.where(valid, 0.0)
        weighted_return = group_ret.fillna(0.0) * used_weight

        total_weight = used_weight.sum(axis=1)
        total_return = weighted_return.sum(axis=1)
        peer_weight = total_weight.to_frame().to_numpy() - used_weight.to_numpy()
        peer_return = total_return.to_frame().to_numpy() - weighted_return.to_numpy()

        basket = peer_return / np.where(peer_weight > 0.0, peer_weight, np.nan)
        basket = pd.DataFrame(basket, index=returns_frame.index, columns=members)
        valid_peers = valid.sum(axis=1).to_frame().to_numpy() - valid.astype(int).to_numpy()
        output.loc[:, members] = basket.where(valid_peers >= 2)

    return output


def _masked_rolling_beta(
    stock_return: pd.DataFrame,
    peer_return: pd.DataFrame,
    mask: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    minimum: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS beta using only observations selected by mask."""
    usable = mask & stock_return.notna() & peer_return.notna()
    count = usable.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).sum()
    x = peer_return.where(usable, 0.0)
    y = stock_return.where(usable, 0.0)

    sx = x.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).sum()
    sy = y.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).sum()
    sxx = (x * x).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).sum()
    sxy = (x * y).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).sum()

    variance_x = sxx - sx * sx / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    covariance_xy = sxy - sx * sy / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = covariance_xy / variance_x.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return beta.where(count >= minimum).clip(-3.0, 3.0)


@register_factor
class DownsideCentralityRecoveryRelayH6(BaseFactor):
    """Newly downside-central sector nodes selected after stress begins to stabilize."""

    factor_id = "downside_centrality_recovery_relay_h6"
    name = "Downside Centrality Recovery Relay"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Longs resilient stocks whose downside-specific leave-one-out sector beta has "
        "recently risen, after a completed peer drawdown has begun to stabilize."
    )
    window_length = 70
    inputs = ["close", "sector", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        sector = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        market_cap = data["marketCap"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        stock_return = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        peer_return = _leave_one_out_cap_weighted_return(stock_return, sector, market_cap)
        valid_pair = stock_return.notna() & peer_return.notna()
        downside_pair = valid_pair & peer_return.lt(0.0)

        ordinary_beta = _masked_rolling_beta(stock_return, peer_return, valid_pair, 63, 40)
        downside_beta = _masked_rolling_beta(stock_return, peer_return, downside_pair, 63, 14)
        downside_excess_beta = (downside_beta - ordinary_beta).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        centrality_migration = (downside_excess_beta - downside_excess_beta.shift(8)).clip(0.0, 1.5)

        peer_scale = peer_return.rolling(42, min_periods=25).std() * np.sqrt(4.0)
        prior_drawdown = -peer_return.shift(2).rolling(4, min_periods=4).sum()
        completed_stress = (prior_drawdown / peer_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 3.0)

        recent_peer_recovery = peer_return.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        recovery_gate = (recent_peer_recovery / (peer_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan) / np.sqrt(2.0))).clip(0.0, 1.5)

        residual_daily = stock_return - ordinary_beta * peer_return
        residual_scale = residual_daily.rolling(42, min_periods=25).std() * np.sqrt(2.0)
        residual_resilience = (
            residual_daily.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
            / residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(0.0, 3.0)

        raw_score = centrality_migration * completed_stress * recovery_gate * residual_resilience
        active_score = raw_score.where(raw_score.gt(0.0))
        return rank(active_score).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(close)

programs.trading_idea: A rise in downside-specific sector loading identifies stocks whose network role becomes more central during a sector stress episode. The prior version's positive six-day IC, despite negative one-to-three-day returns, suggests that these names first face mechanical contagion-related de-risking but subsequently recover when the sector shock stabilizes; conditional relative resilience identifies the nodes most likely to receive this recovery flow. The refined implementation therefore measures a recently elevated downside beta, requires that the sector drawdown occurred before the latest two-bar stabilization, and longs resilient newly central nodes rather than assuming they must immediately sell off.

"""Fundamental repair makes unforecastable thin-volume return shocks reversible.

Mechanism: an unexpectedly large close-to-close move on weak participation is
more likely to be a transient liquidity or opinion-reinforcement displacement
when a firm's operating and financing position is improving. Predictable
volatility is excluded because recurring volatility need not represent a
mispricing that reverts over the next week.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_rank(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional rank with neutral treatment of unavailable fundamentals."""
    clean = value.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return rank(clean).fillna(0.5)


def _unexpected_return_shock(close: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return direction and excess magnitude relative to causal expected volatility."""
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    expected_abs_ret = ret.abs().shift(1).ewm(
        halflife=15, adjust=False, min_periods=20
    ).mean()
    expected_abs_ret = expected_abs_ret.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    standardized_return = (ret / expected_abs_ret).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)
    excess_magnitude = (ret.abs() / expected_abs_ret - 1.0).clip(
        lower=0.0, upper=4.0
    )
    return standardized_return, excess_magnitude


def _thin_volume_score(volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Positive only when current participation is below its trailing norm."""
    log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0))
    mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean()
    scale = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()
    low_volume_z = (mean - log_volume) / scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return low_volume_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0) / 3.0


def _repair_score(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Sparse-data-robust operating, leverage, and cash-value repair anchor."""
    margin = data["operatingMargin"]
    leverage = data["debtToEquity"]
    fcf_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"]

    margin_improvement = margin - margin.shift(63)
    deleveraging = -(leverage - leverage.shift(63))

    repair = (
        _cs_rank(margin_improvement)
        + _cs_rank(deleveraging)
        + _cs_rank(fcf_yield.where(fcf_yield > -1.0))
    ) / 3.0
    return repair


@register_factor
class RepairAnchoredUnforecastableVolatilityFade(BaseFactor):
    """Fade thin-volume unforecastable shocks in fundamentally repairing firms."""

    factor_id = "repair_anchored_unforecastable_volatility_fade"
    name = "Repair-Anchored Volatility Surprise Fade"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional reversal signal for low-volume close-to-close shocks that "
        "exceed expected volatility, weighted by a simple operating, leverage, and "
        "free-cash-flow repair anchor."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "operatingMargin",
        "debtToEquity",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        direction, surprise = _unexpected_return_shock(close)
        thinness = _thin_volume_score(data["volume"])
        repair = _repair_score(data)

        raw = -direction * surprise * thinness * repair
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return _cs_rank(raw).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Repair-Anchored Volatility Surprise Fade
programs.trading_idea: The original premise is retained, but the relevant displacement is a close-to-close return shock that is large relative to the name's own expected volatility, rather than an intraday range whose direction can be ambiguous. In a fundamentally repairing firm, an unexpectedly volatile move on unusually low participation is more likely to reflect a temporary liquidity or opinion-reinforcement episode than a broadly informed repricing, and should reverse over the next week. Predictable high volatility is explicitly excluded: it is recurring risk, not a surprise displacement, and is less likely to mean-revert at the fixed six-day horizon.
programs.description: Fades abnormal close-to-close return shocks only when realized absolute return exceeds trailing expected volatility, volume is unusually low, and operating margin, leverage, and free-cash-flow valuation indicate repair credibility. The signal uses robust trailing normalizations and simple cross-sectional repair ranks.

"""Sector-residual opening-auction liquidity-grab handoff drift.

Mechanism: an opening gap shared by a sector is more likely to reflect common
information.  An idiosyncratic opening displacement that is rejected by an
idiosyncratic opposite regular-session move is more consistent with temporary
auction liquidity pressure and trapped opening inventory.  The regular-session
rejection direction is expected to persist as that inventory is handed off.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_median(frame: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional sector median using the static sector classification."""
    groups = sector.reindex(columns=frame.columns).iloc[0].astype(object)
    fallback = pd.Series(frame.columns, index=frame.columns, dtype=object)
    groups = groups.where(groups.notna(), fallback)
    return frame.T.groupby(groups).transform("median").T


def _idiosyncratic_auction_handoff(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal, sector-residual gap rejection score."""
    prior_close = close.shift(1)
    valid = open_.gt(0.0) & close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0)

    opening_gap = np.log(open_.where(open_.gt(0.0)) / prior_close.where(prior_close.gt(0.0)))
    session_move = np.log(close.where(close.gt(0.0)) / open_.where(open_.gt(0.0)))

    idio_gap = opening_gap - _sector_median(opening_gap, sector)
    idio_session = session_move - _sector_median(session_move, sector)

    close_return = np.log(close.where(close.gt(0.0)) / prior_close.where(prior_close.gt(0.0)))
    volatility = close_return.rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    # Smoothly emphasize material residual auction dislocations without a
    # threshold whose placement can overfit a particular sample.
    gap_strength = np.tanh(idio_gap.abs() / volatility)
    rejected = (idio_gap * idio_session) < 0.0
    score = idio_session * gap_strength

    return score.where(valid & rejected, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class IdiosyncraticAuctionHandoffDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks sector-residual opening-auction rejection handoffs."""

    factor_id = "idiosyncratic_auction_handoff_drift"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Auction Handoff Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Signed sector-relative open-to-close rejection following an opposite-"
        "signed sector-relative opening gap, scaled by trailing-volatility-"
        "normalized gap abnormality."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["open", "close", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        score = _idiosyncratic_auction_handoff(
            data["open"],
            data["close"],
            data["sector"],
        )
        return rank(score).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Idiosyncratic Auction Handoff Drift
programs.trading_idea: Opening gaps caused by broad sector information should be corroborated by peers and are less likely to represent transient auction liquidity pressure. The cleaner liquidity-grab case is an idiosyncratic opening displacement that is subsequently rejected by an idiosyncratic regular-session move in the opposite direction. This isolates trapped opening-auction inventory and unfinished handoff flow from common market or sector news, with the signed regular-session rejection expected to drift over the next six sessions.
programs.description: The signal measures sector-relative opening gaps and sector-relative open-to-close moves, retains only opposite-signed idiosyncratic handoffs, and scales the signed rejection by the abnormality of the opening displacement relative to trailing volatility.
